## Swipeable Card Stack

A deck of cards you swipe away to reveal the next one.

Category: Cards. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Cards/SwipeableCardStack/SwipeableCardStack.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

enum SwipeableCardStackDirection: Equatable, Sendable {
    case left, right

    var sign: CGFloat { self == .left ? -1 : 1 }
}

enum SwipeableCardStackLogic {
    /// Decides where a released card goes from where its momentum would carry it,
    /// so both a long drag and a short flick count, and a flick back cancels.
    static func direction(predictedEnd: CGFloat, width: CGFloat, threshold: CGFloat = 0.35) -> SwipeableCardStackDirection? {
        guard width > 0, abs(predictedEnd) >= width * threshold else { return nil }
        return predictedEnd > 0 ? .right : .left
    }

    /// One swiped card still flying away, the top card and three behind it.
    /// Empty when the deck shrank below the cards already swiped.
    static func positions(top: Int, count: Int, loops: Bool) -> [Int] {
        guard count > 0 else { return [] }
        let start = max(top - 1, 0)
        let end = loops ? top + 4 : min(top + 4, count)
        return start < end ? Array(start..<end) : []
    }
}

/// A deck of cards. Swipe the top one away to reveal the next.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, a swiped card fades out instead of flying away.
struct SwipeableCardStack<Item, Card: View>: View {
    let items: [Item]
    var loops = false
    var threshold: CGFloat = 0.35
    var onSwipe: (Item, SwipeableCardStackDirection) -> Void = { _, _ in }
    @ViewBuilder var card: (Item) -> Card

    @State private var top = 0
    @State private var drag = CGSize.zero
    @State private var lastDirection = SwipeableCardStackDirection.right
    @State private var size = CGSize.zero
    @GestureState private var isDragging = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var width: CGFloat { size.width }

    private var hasTopCard: Bool { !items.isEmpty && (loops || top < items.count) }

    private var positions: [Int] {
        SwipeableCardStackLogic.positions(top: top, count: items.count, loops: loops)
    }

    private var dragProgress: CGFloat {
        min(abs(drag.width) / max(width * threshold, 1), 1)
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            ForEach(positions, id: \.self) { position in
                let depth = max(CGFloat(position - top) - dragProgress, 0)

                card(items[position % items.count])
                    .scaleEffect(1 - depth * 0.06)
                    .offset(offset(of: position, depth: depth))
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(rotation(of: position)))
                    .opacity(position < top || position - top > 2 ? 0 : 1)
                    .zIndex(Double(-position))
                    .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
                    .accessibilityHidden(position != top)
                    .accessibilityAction(named: "Swipe left") { swipe(.left) }
                    .accessibilityAction(named: "Swipe right") { swipe(.right) }
            }
        }
        .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self) { $0.size } action: { size = $0 }
        .contentShape(.rect)
        .gesture(dragGesture)
        .onChange(of: isDragging) { _, dragging in
            if !dragging {
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3)) { drag = .zero }
            }
        }
    }

    private func offset(of position: Int, depth: CGFloat) -> CGSize {
        if position < top {
            return CGSize(width: reduceMotion ? 0 : lastDirection.sign * width * 1.5, height: 0)
        }
        if position == top {
            return CGSize(width: drag.width, height: drag.height * 0.25)
        }
        // Scaling shrinks a card around its center, so move it down by that amount plus the visible peek.
        return CGSize(width: 0, height: depth * (size.height * 0.03 + 14))
    }

    private func rotation(of position: Int) -> Double {
        guard !reduceMotion, width > 0 else { return 0 }
        if position < top { return Double(lastDirection.sign) * 18 }
        return position == top ? Double(drag.width / width) * 14 : 0
    }

    private var dragGesture: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 8)
            .updating($isDragging) { _, state, _ in state = true }
            .onChanged { value in
                if hasTopCard { drag = value.translation }
            }
            .onEnded { value in
                let predictedEnd = value.predictedEndTranslation.width
                if let direction = SwipeableCardStackLogic.direction(predictedEnd: predictedEnd, width: width, threshold: threshold) {
                    swipe(direction)
                }
            }
    }

    private func swipe(_ direction: SwipeableCardStackDirection) {
        guard hasTopCard else { return }
        let item = items[top % items.count]
        withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .snappy(duration: 0.4)) {
            lastDirection = direction
            top += 1
            drag = .zero
        }
        onSwipe(item, direction)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct DemoPlace {
    let name: String
    let symbol: String
    let colors: [Color]
}

struct SwipeableCardStackDemo: View {
    @State private var liked = 0
    @State private var passed = 0

    private let places = [
        DemoPlace(name: "Kyoto", symbol: "leaf.fill", colors: [.pink, .purple]),
        DemoPlace(name: "Reykjavik", symbol: "snowflake", colors: [.cyan, .blue]),
        DemoPlace(name: "Marrakesh", symbol: "sun.max.fill", colors: [.orange, .red]),
        DemoPlace(name: "Lisbon", symbol: "tram.fill", colors: [.yellow, .orange]),
        DemoPlace(name: "Patagonia", symbol: "mountain.2.fill", colors: [.teal, .indigo]),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 28) {
            Text("Where next?")
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

            SwipeableCardStack(items: places, loops: true) { place, direction in
                if direction == .right { liked += 1 } else { passed += 1 }
            } card: { place in
                cardView(for: place)
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 32)
            .frame(maxHeight: 500)
            .padding(.bottom, 32)

            HStack(spacing: 32) {
                Label("\(passed)", systemImage: "xmark")
                    .accessibilityLabel("Passed \(passed)")
                Label("\(liked)", systemImage: "heart.fill")
                    .accessibilityLabel("Liked \(liked)")
            }
            .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))
            .monospacedDigit()
            .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
        .padding(.vertical, 24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo.opacity(0.18), .pink.opacity(0.12)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom))
    }

    private func cardView(for place: DemoPlace) -> some View {
        VStack(spacing: 16) {
            Image(systemName: place.symbol)
                .font(.system(.largeTitle))
                .imageScale(.large)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            Text(place.name)
                .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
        }
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: place.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 32))
        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.18), radius: 14, y: 8)
    }
}

#Preview {
    SwipeableCardStackDemo()
}
```

## Tilt Card

A card that tilts in 3D toward the finger with a moving highlight.

Category: Cards. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Cards/TiltCard/TiltCard.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A card that leans in 3D toward the finger, with a highlight that follows it.
///
/// `restingPoint` is where the card leans while nobody touches it. `nil` keeps it flat.
/// With Reduce Motion on, the card stays flat and only the highlight moves.
struct TiltCard<Content: View>: View {
    var maxAngle: Double = 14
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat = 28
    var restingPoint: UnitPoint?
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @GestureState private var touchPoint: UnitPoint?
    @State private var size = CGSize.zero
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var focus: UnitPoint? { touchPoint ?? restingPoint }

    private var pitch: Double {
        guard let focus, !reduceMotion else { return 0 }
        return (0.5 - focus.y) * 2 * maxAngle
    }

    private var yaw: Double {
        guard let focus, !reduceMotion else { return 0 }
        return (focus.x - 0.5) * 2 * maxAngle
    }

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .overlay { highlight }
            .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self) { $0.size } action: { size = $0 }
            .gesture(tilt)
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.35), radius: 24, y: 16)
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(pitch), axis: (x: 1, y: 0, z: 0), perspective: 0.6)
            .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(yaw), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0), perspective: 0.6)
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3), value: touchPoint)
    }

    private var highlight: some View {
        RadialGradient(
            colors: [.white.opacity(0.35), .white.opacity(0)],
            center: focus ?? .center,
            startRadius: 0,
            endRadius: max(size.width, size.height) * 0.8
        )
        .blendMode(.plusLighter)
        .opacity(focus == nil ? 0 : 1)
        .allowsHitTesting(false)
        .accessibilityHidden(true)
    }

    private var tilt: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
            .updating($touchPoint) { value, state, _ in
                guard size.width > 0, size.height > 0 else { return }
                state = UnitPoint(
                    x: min(max(value.location.x / size.width, 0), 1),
                    y: min(max(value.location.y / size.height, 0), 1)
                )
            }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct TiltCardDemo: View {
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 60.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
                let time = context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * 1.6

                TiltCard(restingPoint: reduceMotion ? nil : UnitPoint(x: 0.5 + 0.45 * cos(time), y: 0.5 + 0.45 * sin(time))) {
                    card
                }
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 44)
        }
    }

    private var card: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
            Image(systemName: "sparkles")
                .font(.largeTitle)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Spacer()

            Text("Aurora Pass")
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            Text("Touch and move your finger")
                .font(.subheadline)
                .opacity(0.8)
        }
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .padding(24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
        .aspectRatio(0.68, contentMode: .fit)
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.purple, .pink, .orange], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }
}

    TiltCardDemo()
}
```

## Counter Stepper

Minus and plus buttons around a number that rolls as it changes and stops at its limits.

Category: Controls. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Controls/CounterStepper/CounterStepper.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

enum CounterStepperValue {
    /// The result of adding `step` to `value`, kept inside `range`.
    static func stepped(_ value: Int, by step: Int, in range: ClosedRange<Int>) -> Int {
        let (sum, overflowed) = value.addingReportingOverflow(step)
        if overflowed {
            return step > 0 ? range.upperBound : range.lowerBound
        }
        return min(max(sum, range.lowerBound), range.upperBound)
    }

    static func canStep(_ value: Int, by step: Int, in range: ClosedRange<Int>) -> Bool {
        stepped(value, by: step, in: range) != value
    }
}

/// Minus and plus buttons around a number that rolls as it changes.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the number changes without rolling.
struct CounterStepper: View {
    @Binding var value: Int
    var range: ClosedRange<Int> = 0...99
    var step: Int = 1
    var title: String = "Value"
    var tint: Color = .indigo

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title) private var buttonSize = 56.0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var numberWidth = 76.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 6) {
            stepButton(systemImage: "minus", label: "Decrease", delta: -step)

            Text(value, format: .number)
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .monospacedDigit()
                .contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .numericText(value: Double(value)))
                .frame(minWidth: numberWidth)
                .accessibilityLabel(title)
                .accessibilityValue(value.formatted())

            stepButton(systemImage: "plus", label: "Increase", delta: step)
        }
        .padding(6)
        .background(.quaternary, in: .capsule)
        .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: value)
    }

    private func stepButton(systemImage: String, label: String, delta: Int) -> some View {
        let isEnabled = CounterStepperValue.canStep(value, by: delta, in: range)

        return Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy) {
                value = CounterStepperValue.stepped(value, by: delta, in: range)
            }
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: systemImage)
                .font(.title2.bold())
                .foregroundStyle(isEnabled ? Color.white : Color.secondary)
                .frame(width: buttonSize, height: buttonSize)
                .background(isEnabled ? tint : Color.gray.opacity(0.2), in: .circle)
                .contentShape(.circle)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .disabled(!isEnabled)
        .accessibilityLabel(label)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CounterStepperDemo: View {
    @State private var tickets = 3
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var total: Int { tickets * 24 }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 32) {
            VStack(spacing: 6) {
                Text("Tickets")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                Text(total, format: .currency(code: "EUR").precision(.fractionLength(0)))
                    .font(.title2.weight(.semibold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .numericText(value: Double(total)))
            }
            .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)

            CounterStepper(value: $tickets, range: 0...5, title: "Tickets")
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
    }
}

#Preview {
    CounterStepperDemo()
}
```

## Sliding Segmented Picker

A segmented picker whose selected pill glides between the options.

Category: Controls. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Controls/SlidingSegmentedPicker/SlidingSegmentedPicker.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A segmented picker whose selected pill glides between the options.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the pill moves without animating.
struct SlidingSegmentedPicker<Option: Hashable>: View {
    @Binding var selection: Option
    let options: [Option]
    var tint: Color = .indigo
    let title: (Option) -> String

    @Namespace private var namespace
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 4) {
            ForEach(options, id: \.self) { option in
                let isSelected = option == selection

                Button {
                    selection = option
                } label: {
                    Text(title(option))
                        .font(.headline)
                        .lineLimit(1)
                        .minimumScaleFactor(0.7)
                        .foregroundStyle(isSelected ? Color.white : Color.primary)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                        .padding(.vertical, 14)
                        .background {
                            if isSelected {
                                Capsule()
                                    .fill(tint.gradient)
                                    .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "pill", in: namespace)
                            }
                        }
                        .contentShape(.capsule)
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
                .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
            }
        }
        .padding(4)
        .background(.quaternary, in: .capsule)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.25), value: selection)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SlidingSegmentedPickerDemo: View {
    private enum Period: String, CaseIterable {
        case day = "Day"
        case week = "Week"
        case month = "Month"
        case year = "Year"

        var steps: Int {
            switch self {
            case .day: 8_240
            case .week: 54_910
            case .month: 231_075
            case .year: 2_904_330
            }
        }
    }

    @State private var period = Period.day
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 36) {
            VStack(spacing: 6) {
                Text(period.steps, format: .number)
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                    .contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .numericText(value: Double(period.steps)))
                Text("steps walked")
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
            .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)

            SlidingSegmentedPicker(selection: $period, options: Period.allCases) { $0.rawValue }
        }
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy, value: period)
        .padding(24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
    }
}
```

## Spring Toggle Style

A custom toggle style whose knob widens under the finger and overshoots as it lands.

Category: Controls. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Controls/SpringToggleStyle/SpringToggleStyle.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A toggle whose knob widens under your finger and overshoots as it lands.
/// The whole row is tappable, and VoiceOver reads it as a standard switch.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the knob slides without bouncing or widening.
struct SpringToggleStyle: ToggleStyle {
    var onColor: Color = .green

    func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
        Button {
            configuration.isOn.toggle()
        } label: {
            configuration.label
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                .contentShape(.rect)
        }
        .buttonStyle(SpringToggleStyleRow(isOn: configuration.isOn, onColor: onColor))
        .accessibilityRepresentation {
            Toggle(isOn: configuration.$isOn) {
                configuration.label
            }
        }
    }
}

extension ToggleStyle where Self == SpringToggleStyle {
    static var spring: SpringToggleStyle { SpringToggleStyle() }
}

private struct SpringToggleStyleRow: ButtonStyle {
    let isOn: Bool
    let onColor: Color

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var trackHeight = 34.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let knobInset = 3.0

    private var animation: Animation {
        reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.15) : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.55)
    }

    func makeBody(configuration: Configuration) -> some View {
        let isSquashed = configuration.isPressed && !reduceMotion
        let knobHeight = trackHeight - knobInset * 2

        HStack(spacing: 16) {
            configuration.label

            Capsule()
                .fill(isOn ? onColor : Color.gray.opacity(0.35))
                .frame(width: trackHeight * 1.75, height: trackHeight)
                .overlay(alignment: isOn ? .trailing : .leading) {
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(.white)
                        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 3, y: 2)
                        .frame(width: isSquashed ? knobHeight * 1.3 : knobHeight, height: knobHeight)
                        .padding(knobInset)
                }
        }
        .animation(animation, value: isOn)
        .animation(animation, value: isSquashed)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SpringToggleStyleDemo: View {
    @State private var notifications = false
    @State private var sounds = true
    @State private var haptics = false

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 28) {
            Toggle(isOn: $notifications) { Label("Notifications", systemImage: "bell.fill") }
            Toggle(isOn: $sounds) { Label("Sounds", systemImage: "speaker.wave.2.fill") }
            Toggle(isOn: $haptics) { Label("Haptics", systemImage: "iphone.radiowaves.left.and.right") }
        }
        .toggleStyle(.spring)
        .font(.title3.weight(.medium))
        .padding(24)
        .background(.background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 28))
        .padding(20)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(uiColor: .systemGroupedBackground).ignoresSafeArea())
    }
}

#Preview {
    SpringToggleStyleDemo()
}
```

## Swipe To Confirm Slider

A track with a thumb you drag to the end to confirm, which springs back if released early.

Category: Controls. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Controls/SwipeToConfirmSlider/SwipeToConfirmSlider.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

enum SwipeToConfirmSliderMath {
    /// How far along its travel the thumb is, from 0 to 1.
    static func progress(translation: Double, trackWidth: Double, thumbWidth: Double) -> Double {
        let travel = trackWidth - thumbWidth
        guard travel > 0 else { return 0 }
        return min(max(translation / travel, 0), 1)
    }

    static func thumbOffset(progress: Double, trackWidth: Double, thumbWidth: Double) -> Double {
        max(trackWidth - thumbWidth, 0) * min(max(progress, 0), 1)
    }

    static func isConfirmed(progress: Double, threshold: Double = 0.92) -> Bool {
        progress >= threshold
    }
}

/// A track with a thumb you drag to the end to confirm. Letting go early springs it back.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the thumb returns without bouncing. VoiceOver users
/// confirm with a double tap.
struct SwipeToConfirmSlider: View {
    let title: String
    var confirmedTitle: String = "Confirmed"
    var tint: Color = .indigo
    var resetDelay: Double = 1.4
    let onConfirm: () -> Void

    @State private var progress = 0.0
    @State private var isConfirmed = false
    @GestureState private var isDragging = false
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title3) private var height = 68.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let inset = 5.0

    private var settle: Animation {
        reduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.15) : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.35)
    }

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            let trackWidth = proxy.size.width - inset * 2
            let thumbWidth = height - inset * 2
            let offset = SwipeToConfirmSliderMath.thumbOffset(
                progress: progress,
                trackWidth: trackWidth,
                thumbWidth: thumbWidth
            )

            ZStack(alignment: .leading) {
                Capsule()
                    .fill(.quaternary)

                Capsule()
                    .fill(tint.gradient)
                    .frame(width: offset + height)

                Text(isConfirmed ? confirmedTitle : title)
                    .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))
                    .lineLimit(1)
                    .minimumScaleFactor(0.7)
                    .foregroundStyle(isConfirmed ? Color.white : Color.primary)
                    .opacity(isConfirmed ? 1 : max(1 - progress * 1.6, 0))
                    .padding(.horizontal, height)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)

                Image(systemName: isConfirmed ? "checkmark" : "chevron.right.2")
                    .font(.title3.bold())
                    .foregroundStyle(tint)
                    .contentTransition(reduceMotion ? .identity : .symbolEffect(.replace))
                    .frame(width: thumbWidth, height: thumbWidth)
                    .background(.white, in: .circle)
                    .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.2), radius: 5, y: 3)
                    .contentShape(.circle)
                    .offset(x: inset + offset)
                    .gesture(drag(trackWidth: trackWidth, thumbWidth: thumbWidth))
            }
        }
        .frame(height: height)
        .onChange(of: isDragging) { _, dragging in
            guard !dragging, !isConfirmed else { return }
            withAnimation(settle) { progress = 0 }
        }
        .sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: isConfirmed) { _, confirmed in confirmed }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(isConfirmed ? confirmedTitle : title)
        .accessibilityHint("Double tap to confirm")
        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)
        .accessibilityAction { confirm() }
    }

    private func drag(trackWidth: Double, thumbWidth: Double) -> some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0)
            .updating($isDragging) { _, state, _ in state = true }
            .onChanged { value in
                guard !isConfirmed else { return }
                progress = SwipeToConfirmSliderMath.progress(
                    translation: value.translation.width,
                    trackWidth: trackWidth,
                    thumbWidth: thumbWidth
                )
            }
            .onEnded { _ in
                if SwipeToConfirmSliderMath.isConfirmed(progress: progress) {
                    confirm()
                }
            }
    }

    private func confirm() {
        guard !isConfirmed else { return }
        withAnimation(settle) {
            progress = 1
            isConfirmed = true
        }
        onConfirm()

        Task {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(resetDelay))
            withAnimation(settle) {
                progress = 0
                isConfirmed = false
            }
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SwipeToConfirmSliderDemo: View {
    @State private var payments = 0

    var body: some View {
        SwipeToConfirmSlider(title: "Slide to pay") {
            payments += 1
        }
        .padding(.horizontal, 24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .overlay(alignment: .top) {
            VStack(spacing: 6) {
                Text("48.00 €")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                Text(payments == 1 ? "1 payment sent" : "\(payments) payments sent")
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }
            .padding(.top, 72)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    SwipeToConfirmSliderDemo()
}
```

## Confetti Burst

A one-shot confetti burst with simple physics, fired by changing a trigger.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/ConfettiBurst/ConfettiBurst.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Fires a one-shot burst of confetti every time `trigger` changes.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the pieces appear scattered and fade out without moving.
struct ConfettiBurst: ViewModifier {
    var trigger: Int
    var count: Int = 120
    /// Where the burst starts, as a fraction of the view.
    var origin: UnitPoint = UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0.68)
    var colors: [Color] = [.pink, .yellow, .mint, .cyan, .orange, .purple]
    var lifetime: Double = 3

    @State private var start: Date?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private static let motion = ConfettiBurstMotion()

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                TimelineView(.animation(paused: start == nil)) { timeline in
                    Canvas { context, size in
                        guard let start else { return }
                        draw(elapsed: timeline.date.timeIntervalSince(start), in: context, size: size)
                    }
                }
                .ignoresSafeArea()
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .onChange(of: trigger) { start = .now }
            .task(id: start) {
                guard start != nil else { return }
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(lifetime))
                if !Task.isCancelled { start = nil }
            }
    }

    private func draw(elapsed: Double, in context: GraphicsContext, size: CGSize) {
        guard elapsed < lifetime, !colors.isEmpty else { return }

        let time = reduceMotion ? 0.6 : elapsed
        let fade = min((lifetime - elapsed) / (lifetime * 0.3), 1)

        for index in 0..<count {
            let offset = Self.motion.offset(
                // Two random values added together cluster the pieces around straight up.
                angle: (noise(index, 1) + noise(index, 7) - 1) * 0.9,
                speed: 500 + noise(index, 2) * 1900,
                at: time
            )

            var piece = context
            piece.opacity = fade
            piece.translateBy(x: origin.x * size.width + offset.x, y: origin.y * size.height + offset.y)
            piece.rotate(by: .radians(time * (noise(index, 3) * 8 - 4) + noise(index, 4) * 2 * .pi))
            piece.scaleBy(x: cos(time * (4 + noise(index, 5) * 8) + noise(index, 6) * 2 * .pi), y: 1)

            let color = GraphicsContext.Shading.color(colors[index % colors.count])
            if index.isMultiple(of: 3) {
                piece.fill(Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: -4, y: -4, width: 8, height: 8)), with: color)
            } else {
                piece.fill(Path(CGRect(x: -4, y: -6.5, width: 8, height: 13)), with: color)
            }
        }
    }

    /// A repeatable pseudo-random value in 0..<1, different for each burst.
    private func noise(_ index: Int, _ salt: Double) -> Double {
        let value = sin(Double(index) * 127.1 + (salt + Double(trigger) * 0.37) * 311.7) * 43758.5453
        return value - floor(value)
    }
}

/// The flight of one piece: thrown from the origin, slowed by air and pulled down by gravity.
struct ConfettiBurstMotion {
    /// Points per second squared.
    var gravity: Double = 900
    /// How quickly air slows a piece, per second.
    var drag: Double = 2.6

    /// The offset from the origin, with y growing downward.
    /// - Parameters:
    ///   - angle: The launch direction in radians: 0 is straight up, positive leans right.
    ///   - speed: The launch speed in points per second.
    ///   - time: The seconds since launch.
    func offset(angle: Double, speed: Double, at time: Double) -> CGPoint {
        let time = max(time, 0)
        let drag = max(drag, 0.001)
        let travelled = (1 - exp(-drag * time)) / drag

        return CGPoint(
            x: sin(angle) * speed * travelled,
            y: -cos(angle) * speed * travelled + gravity / drag * (time - travelled)
        )
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Fires a one-shot burst of confetti over this view every time `trigger` changes.
    func confettiBurst(trigger: Int, count: Int = 120, origin: UnitPoint = UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0.68)) -> some View {
        modifier(ConfettiBurst(trigger: trigger, count: count, origin: origin))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ConfettiBurstDemo: View {
    @State private var bursts = 0

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [Color(red: 0.13, green: 0.09, blue: 0.33), Color(red: 0.36, green: 0.13, blue: 0.45)],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )
            .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                Spacer()

                Image(systemName: "trophy.fill")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, weight: .bold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.yellow)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("You Did It")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)

                Spacer()

                Button("Celebrate") { bursts += 1 }
                    .font(.headline)
                    .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                    .controlSize(.large)
                    .tint(.pink)
                    .padding(.bottom, 32)
            }
        }
        .confettiBurst(trigger: bursts)
        .task {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.3))
            bursts += 1
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ConfettiBurstDemo()
}
```

## Noise Grain Overlay

A view modifier that lays a subtle animated film grain over any view.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/NoiseGrainOverlay/NoiseGrainOverlay.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A subtle film grain over any view: tiny light and dark specks redrawn a few times a second.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the grain is still.
struct NoiseGrainOverlay: ViewModifier {
    var intensity: Double = 0.16
    var grainSize: Double = 1.25
    var framesPerSecond: Double = 12

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    /// A tiny seeded generator: the same frame number always gives the same grain.
    private struct Generator: RandomNumberGenerator {
        var state: UInt64

        mutating func next() -> UInt64 {
            state ^= state << 13
            state ^= state >> 7
            state ^= state << 17
            return state
        }
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.overlay {
            TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1 / framesPerSecond, paused: reduceMotion)) { timeline in
                Canvas { context, size in
                    let frame = reduceMotion ? 0 : UInt64(timeline.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * framesPerSecond)
                    drawGrain(frame: frame, in: context, size: size)
                }
            }
            .allowsHitTesting(false)
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
    }

    /// Every speck goes into one of two paths, so a frame is only two fills.
    private func drawGrain(frame: UInt64, in context: GraphicsContext, size: CGSize) {
        var generator = Generator(state: (frame &+ 1) &* 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15)
        var light = Path()
        var dark = Path()

        for index in 0..<min(Int(size.width * size.height / 18), 20_000) {
            let speck = CGRect(
                x: Double.random(in: 0..<max(size.width, 1), using: &generator),
                y: Double.random(in: 0..<max(size.height, 1), using: &generator),
                width: grainSize,
                height: grainSize
            )
            if index.isMultiple(of: 2) {
                light.addRect(speck)
            } else {
                dark.addRect(speck)
            }
        }

        context.fill(light, with: .color(.white.opacity(intensity)))
        context.fill(dark, with: .color(.black.opacity(intensity)))
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Adds a subtle animated film grain on top of this view.
    func noiseGrainOverlay(intensity: Double = 0.16, grainSize: Double = 1.25) -> some View {
        modifier(NoiseGrainOverlay(intensity: intensity, grainSize: grainSize))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct NoiseGrainOverlayDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink, .indigo], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .noiseGrainOverlay(intensity: 0.22)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) {
                Image(systemName: "film")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("Golden Hour")
                    .font(.system(.title, design: .serif, weight: .bold))
                Text("Grain takes the digital edge off flat color.")
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.85))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .padding(24)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 260, alignment: .bottomLeading)
            .background(Color(red: 0.16, green: 0.12, blue: 0.3))
            .noiseGrainOverlay(intensity: 0.15)
            .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 28))
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.35), radius: 24, y: 12)
            .padding(28)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    NoiseGrainOverlayDemo()
}
```

## Ripple Tap Effect

A view modifier that spawns an expanding ripple wherever the user taps.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/RippleTapEffect/RippleTapEffect.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Spawns an expanding ripple wherever the user taps, without blocking the view's own controls.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, a ripple fades in place instead of expanding.
struct RippleTapEffect: ViewModifier {
    var color: Color = .white
    var maxRadius: Double = 170
    var duration: Double = 0.9
    var cornerRadius: Double = 0

    private struct Ripple: Identifiable {
        let id = UUID()
        let location: CGPoint
        let start: Date
    }

    @State private var ripples: [Ripple] = []
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay {
                TimelineView(.animation(paused: ripples.isEmpty)) { timeline in
                    Canvas { context, _ in
                        for ripple in ripples {
                            draw(ripple, at: timeline.date, in: context)
                        }
                    }
                }
                .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
            }
            .contentShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
            .simultaneousGesture(SpatialTapGesture().onEnded { spawn(at: $0.location) })
    }

    private func spawn(at location: CGPoint) {
        let ripple = Ripple(location: location, start: .now)
        ripples.append(ripple)

        Task {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(duration))
            ripples.removeAll { $0.id == ripple.id }
        }
    }

    private func draw(_ ripple: Ripple, at date: Date, in context: GraphicsContext) {
        let progress = min(max(date.timeIntervalSince(ripple.start) / duration, 0), 1)
        let eased = 1 - pow(1 - progress, 3)
        let fade = 1 - progress

        for (scale, width) in [(1.0, 2.5), (0.62, 1.5)] {
            let radius = (reduceMotion ? 0.45 : eased) * maxRadius * scale
            let circle = Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(
                x: ripple.location.x - radius,
                y: ripple.location.y - radius,
                width: radius * 2,
                height: radius * 2
            ))
            context.fill(circle, with: .color(color.opacity(0.1 * fade)))
            context.stroke(circle, with: .color(color.opacity(0.75 * fade)), lineWidth: width)
        }
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Spawns a ripple at every tap on this view.
    func rippleTapEffect(color: Color = .white, maxRadius: Double = 170, cornerRadius: Double = 0) -> some View {
        modifier(RippleTapEffect(color: color, maxRadius: maxRadius, cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct RippleTapEffectDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(
                colors: [.teal, .blue, Color(red: 0.14, green: 0.1, blue: 0.45)],
                startPoint: .top,
                endPoint: .bottom
            )

            VStack(spacing: 10) {
                Image(systemName: "hand.tap.fill")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)
                Text("Tap Anywhere")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
        .rippleTapEffect()
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    }
}

#Preview {
    RippleTapEffectDemo()
}
```

## Spotlight Overlay

A dark overlay with a soft hole that follows the finger.

Category: Effects. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Effects/SpotlightOverlay/SpotlightOverlay.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A dark overlay with a soft hole that follows the finger.
///
/// The hole only moves with the finger, so it needs no change for Reduce Motion.
struct SpotlightOverlay: ViewModifier {
    /// The center of the hole, as a fraction of the view.
    @Binding var center: UnitPoint
    var radius: Double = 130
    /// How much of the radius is the soft edge, from 0 to 1.
    var softness: Double = 0.55
    var dimming: Color = .black.opacity(0.88)

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.overlay {
            GeometryReader { proxy in
                // Past its end radius the gradient keeps its last color, so one fill is both the hole and the dark.
                Rectangle()
                    .fill(RadialGradient(
                        stops: [
                            .init(color: dimming.opacity(0), location: 1 - softness),
                            .init(color: dimming, location: 1),
                        ],
                        center: center,
                        startRadius: 0,
                        endRadius: radius
                    ))
                    .contentShape(.rect)
                    .gesture(DragGesture(minimumDistance: 0).onChanged { value in
                        center = UnitPoint(
                            x: value.location.x / max(proxy.size.width, 1),
                            y: value.location.y / max(proxy.size.height, 1)
                        )
                    })
            }
            .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Darkens this view except for a soft hole at `center`, which follows the finger.
    func spotlightOverlay(
        center: Binding<UnitPoint>,
        radius: Double = 130,
        softness: Double = 0.55,
        dimming: Color = .black.opacity(0.88)
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(SpotlightOverlay(center: center, radius: radius, softness: softness, dimming: dimming))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SpotlightOverlayDemo: View {
    @State private var center = UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0.45)
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let symbols = [
        "star.fill", "heart.fill", "bolt.fill", "leaf.fill", "flame.fill", "drop.fill", "moon.fill",
        "sun.max.fill", "cloud.fill", "snowflake", "key.fill", "crown.fill", "gift.fill", "bell.fill",
        "camera.fill", "music.note", "paperplane.fill", "globe.americas.fill", "pawprint.fill", "fish.fill",
        "tortoise.fill", "hare.fill", "ladybug.fill", "ant.fill", "sparkles", "diamond.fill", "gamecontroller.fill",
        "airplane",
    ]
    private let palette: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .yellow, .mint, .teal, .blue, .purple]

    /// Lets a finger take over from the automatic movement.
    private var touchCenter: Binding<UnitPoint> {
        Binding(
            get: { center },
            set: { newValue in
                isAutoPlaying = false
                center = newValue
            }
        )
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color(red: 0.08, green: 0.08, blue: 0.16)

            LazyVGrid(columns: Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: 12), count: 4), spacing: 12) {
                ForEach(symbols.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                    RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 18)
                        .fill(palette[index % palette.count].gradient)
                        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
                        .overlay {
                            Image(systemName: symbols[index])
                                .font(.title)
                                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        }
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                }
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 16)
        }
        .spotlightOverlay(center: touchCenter)
        .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
            Text("Drag to explore")
                .font(.headline)
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .padding(.bottom, 44)
                .allowsHitTesting(false)
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
        .task(id: reduceMotion) { await autoPlay() }
    }

    /// Only the demo moves the hole by itself, until the first touch.
    private func autoPlay() async {
        guard !reduceMotion else { return }

        let start = Date.now
        while isAutoPlaying, !Task.isCancelled {
            let time = Date.now.timeIntervalSince(start)
            center = UnitPoint(x: 0.5 + 0.3 * sin(time * 1.7), y: 0.45 + 0.27 * sin(time * 1.1 + 0.6))
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(16))
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    SpotlightOverlayDemo()
}
```

## Rating Stars

Tappable rating stars that pop with a spring and work as an adjustable value in VoiceOver.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/RatingStars/RatingStars.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

enum RatingStarsValue {
    /// Keeps a rating between zero and the number of stars.
    static func clamped(_ rating: Int, maximum: Int) -> Int {
        min(max(rating, 0), max(maximum, 0))
    }
}

/// A row of tappable stars. Each star pops with a spring when it fills.
///
/// VoiceOver treats the row as one adjustable value. With Reduce Motion on, the stars only change color.
struct RatingStars: View {
    @Binding var rating: Int
    var maximum: Int = 5
    var color: Color = .orange

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 10) {
            ForEach(1...max(maximum, 1), id: \.self) { star in
                starButton(star)
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel("Rating")
        .accessibilityValue("\(rating) of \(maximum) stars")
        .accessibilityAdjustableAction { direction in
            switch direction {
            case .increment: rating = RatingStarsValue.clamped(rating + 1, maximum: maximum)
            case .decrement: rating = RatingStarsValue.clamped(rating - 1, maximum: maximum)
            @unknown default: break
            }
        }
    }

    private func starButton(_ star: Int) -> some View {
        let isFilled = star <= rating

        return Button {
            rating = RatingStarsValue.clamped(star, maximum: maximum)
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: "star.fill")
                .font(.largeTitle)
                .foregroundStyle(isFilled ? AnyShapeStyle(color.gradient) : AnyShapeStyle(.quaternary))
                .animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.15), value: isFilled)
                .phaseAnimator([1.0, 1.4], trigger: isFilled) { view, scale in
                    view.scaleEffect(isFilled && !reduceMotion ? scale : 1)
                } animation: { scale in
                    scale > 1 ? .easeOut(duration: 0.1) : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.6)
                }
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct RatingStarsDemo: View {
    @State private var rating = 0
    @State private var isAutoPlaying = true

    /// Any change made by the user, by touch or VoiceOver, ends the automatic rating.
    private var userRating: Binding<Int> {
        Binding(
            get: { rating },
            set: { newValue in
                isAutoPlaying = false
                rating = newValue
            }
        )
    }

    private var caption: String {
        ["Tap a star", "Terrible", "Not great", "It was fine", "Really good", "Loved it"][rating]
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange.opacity(0.25), .pink.opacity(0.2)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                Image(systemName: "fork.knife.circle.fill")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded))
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .foregroundStyle(.orange.gradient)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text("How was your dinner?")
                    .font(.title2.bold())

                RatingStars(rating: userRating)

                Text(caption)
                    .font(.headline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    .contentTransition(.opacity)
                    .animation(.default, value: rating)
            }
            .padding(32)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 28))
            .padding(24)
        }
        .task(id: isAutoPlaying) {
            guard isAutoPlaying else { return }
            let script = [3, 5, 2, 4]
            var step = 0
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.9))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                rating = script[step % script.count]
                step += 1
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    RatingStarsDemo()
}
```

## Shake Error Modifier

A modifier that shakes a view with keyframes whenever a trigger value changes.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/ShakeErrorModifier/ShakeErrorModifier.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Shakes a view sideways each time `trigger` changes, with an error haptic.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the view stays still and only the haptic plays, so also show the error some other way.
struct ShakeErrorModifier<Trigger: Equatable & Sendable>: ViewModifier {
    let trigger: Trigger
    var distance: CGFloat = 10

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        let distance = reduceMotion ? 0 : distance

        content
            .keyframeAnimator(initialValue: CGFloat.zero, trigger: trigger) { view, offset in
                view.offset(x: offset)
            } keyframes: { _ in
                KeyframeTrack {
                    LinearKeyframe(-distance, duration: 0.06)
                    LinearKeyframe(distance, duration: 0.1)
                    LinearKeyframe(-distance * 0.7, duration: 0.1)
                    LinearKeyframe(distance * 0.5, duration: 0.08)
                    SpringKeyframe(0, duration: 0.2, spring: .bouncy)
                }
            }
            .sensoryFeedback(.error, trigger: trigger)
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Shakes the view each time `trigger` changes.
    func shakeError(trigger: some Equatable & Sendable, distance: CGFloat = 10) -> some View {
        modifier(ShakeErrorModifier(trigger: trigger, distance: distance))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ShakeErrorModifierDemo: View {
    @State private var email = "hello@"
    @State private var attempts = 0
    @State private var showsError = false

    private var isValid: Bool { email.contains("@") && email.contains(".") }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.pink.opacity(0.2), .orange.opacity(0.2)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 14) {
                Text("Join the beta")
                    .font(.title.bold())

                TextField("Email", text: $email)
                    .textContentType(.emailAddress)
                    .keyboardType(.emailAddress)
                    .textInputAutocapitalization(.never)
                    .autocorrectionDisabled()
                    .padding(16)
                    .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 14))
                    .overlay {
                        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 14)
                            .strokeBorder(showsError ? Color.red : Color.clear, lineWidth: 2)
                    }
                    .shakeError(trigger: attempts)

                Text("Enter a complete email address.")
                    .font(.footnote)
                    .foregroundStyle(.red)
                    .opacity(showsError ? 1 : 0)
                    .accessibilityHidden(!showsError)

                Button(action: submit) {
                    Text("Submit")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                        .padding(.vertical, 16)
                        .background(.pink.gradient, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 14))
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
        .onChange(of: email) { showsError = false }
    }

    private func submit() {
        showsError = !isValid
        if !isValid { attempts += 1 }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ShakeErrorModifierDemo()
}
```

## Toast Banner

A toast modifier that slides a banner from the top, announces it to VoiceOver and dismisses by itself.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/ToastBanner/ToastBanner.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// The capsule shown by the `.toast(isPresented:)` modifier.
struct ToastBanner: View {
    let message: String
    var systemImage: String = "checkmark.circle.fill"
    var tint: Color = .green

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 10) {
            Image(systemName: systemImage)
                .font(.title3)
                .foregroundStyle(tint.gradient)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Text(message)
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
        }
        .padding(.horizontal, 20)
        .padding(.vertical, 14)
        .background(.regularMaterial, in: .capsule)
        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.15), radius: 14, y: 6)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
    }
}

private struct ToastBannerModifier: ViewModifier {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    let message: String
    let systemImage: String
    let tint: Color
    let duration: Double

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay(alignment: .top) {
                if isPresented {
                    ToastBanner(message: message, systemImage: systemImage, tint: tint)
                        .padding(.top, 8)
                        .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .move(edge: .top).combined(with: .opacity))
                        .task(id: message) { await announceAndDismiss() }
                }
            }
            .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.3), value: isPresented)
    }

    private func announceAndDismiss() async {
        AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(message).post()
        do {
            try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(duration))
        } catch {
            return
        }
        isPresented = false
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Slides a banner in from the top, announces it to VoiceOver and dismisses it after `duration` seconds.
    ///
    /// With Reduce Motion on, the banner fades instead of sliding.
    func toast(
        isPresented: Binding<Bool>,
        message: String,
        systemImage: String = "checkmark.circle.fill",
        tint: Color = .green,
        duration: Double = 2.2
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(ToastBannerModifier(
            isPresented: isPresented,
            message: message,
            systemImage: systemImage,
            tint: tint,
            duration: duration
        ))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ToastBannerDemo: View {
    @State private var showsToast = false

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.mint.opacity(0.35), .teal.opacity(0.25)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 28) {
                Image(systemName: "doc.text.fill")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .foregroundStyle(.teal.gradient)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text("Quarterly notes")
                    .font(.title2.bold())

                Button {
                    showsToast = true
                } label: {
                    Text("Save")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .padding(.horizontal, 48)
                        .padding(.vertical, 16)
                        .background(.teal.gradient, in: .capsule)
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
            }
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        }
        .toast(isPresented: $showsToast, message: "Changes saved")
    }
}

#Preview {
    ToastBannerDemo()
}
```

## Undo Snackbar

A bottom bar with an Undo button and a shrinking timer line.

Category: Feedback. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Feedback/UndoSnackbar/UndoSnackbar.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A bottom bar with an Undo button and a line that shrinks until the bar expires.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the line stays still and the bar simply fades away on time.
struct UndoSnackbar: View {
    let message: String
    var duration: Double = 5
    var tint: Color = .yellow
    let onUndo: () -> Void
    let onExpire: () -> Void

    @State private var remaining = 1.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @Environment(\.accessibilityVoiceOverEnabled) private var voiceOverEnabled

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 12) {
            Text(message)
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.medium))
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)

            Button(action: onUndo) {
                Text("Undo")
                    .font(.subheadline.bold())
                    .foregroundStyle(tint)
                    .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44)
                    .contentShape(.rect)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
        }
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .padding(.horizontal, 18)
        .padding(.vertical, 6)
        .background(.black.opacity(0.85))
        .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
            Rectangle()
                .fill(tint)
                .frame(height: 3)
                .scaleEffect(x: remaining, anchor: .leading)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)
        }
        .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 16))
        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.2), radius: 14, y: 6)
        .task { await runTimer() }
    }

    private func runTimer() async {
        AccessibilityNotification.Announcement("\(message). Undo available.").post()
        let seconds = voiceOverEnabled ? duration * 2 : duration
        if !reduceMotion {
            withAnimation(.linear(duration: seconds)) { remaining = 0 }
        }
        do {
            try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(seconds))
        } catch {
            return
        }
        onExpire()
    }
}

private struct UndoSnackbarModifier: ViewModifier {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    let message: String
    let duration: Double
    let onUndo: () -> Void

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .overlay(alignment: .bottom) {
                if isPresented {
                    UndoSnackbar(message: message, duration: duration) {
                        isPresented = false
                        onUndo()
                    } onExpire: {
                        isPresented = false
                    }
                    .padding(.horizontal, 16)
                    .padding(.bottom, 12)
                    .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .move(edge: .bottom).combined(with: .opacity))
                }
            }
            .animation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.2), value: isPresented)
    }
}

extension View {
    /// Shows an `UndoSnackbar` at the bottom for `duration` seconds.
    func undoSnackbar(
        isPresented: Binding<Bool>,
        message: String,
        duration: Double = 5,
        onUndo: @escaping () -> Void
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(UndoSnackbarModifier(isPresented: isPresented, message: message, duration: duration, onUndo: onUndo))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct UndoSnackbarDemo: View {
    private static let allMessages = ["Team lunch on Friday", "Your flight is confirmed", "Invoice for October"]

    @State private var messages = allMessages
    @State private var lastArchived: String?
    @State private var showsSnackbar = false

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.blue.opacity(0.25), .indigo.opacity(0.2)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                HStack {
                    Text("Inbox")
                        .font(.largeTitle.bold())

                    Spacer()

                    Button("Archive", systemImage: "archivebox.fill", action: archive)
                        .font(.headline)
                        .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
                        .disabled(showsSnackbar)
                }
                .padding(.bottom, 10)

                ForEach(messages, id: \.self) { message in
                    Label(message, systemImage: "envelope.fill")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .padding(18)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                        .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 16))
                        .transition(.opacity)
                }

                Spacer()
            }
            .padding(24)
            .animation(.smooth, value: messages)
        }
        .undoSnackbar(isPresented: $showsSnackbar, message: "Conversation archived", duration: 3) {
            if let lastArchived { messages.insert(lastArchived, at: 0) }
        }
    }

    private func archive() {
        if messages.isEmpty { messages = Self.allMessages }
        lastArchived = messages.removeFirst()
        showsSnackbar = true
    }
}

#Preview {
    UndoSnackbarDemo()
}
```

## Pinch Zoom View

A view you pinch to zoom and drag, which springs back to its bounds.

Category: Gestures. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Gestures/PinchZoomView/PinchZoomView.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

enum PinchZoomViewMath {
    static func clamp(_ value: CGFloat, to range: ClosedRange<CGFloat>) -> CGFloat {
        min(max(value, range.lowerBound), range.upperBound)
    }

    /// Follows the value inside the range and resists beyond it, so a gesture can overshoot a little.
    static func rubberBand(_ value: CGFloat, in range: ClosedRange<CGFloat>, resistance: CGFloat = 0.3) -> CGFloat {
        let limit = clamp(value, to: range)
        return limit + (value - limit) * resistance
    }

    /// How far content filling its container can move before showing an empty edge.
    static func maxOffset(scale: CGFloat, size: CGSize) -> CGSize {
        CGSize(width: max((scale - 1) * size.width / 2, 0), height: max((scale - 1) * size.height / 2, 0))
    }

    static func clampedOffset(_ offset: CGSize, scale: CGFloat, size: CGSize) -> CGSize {
        let limit = maxOffset(scale: scale, size: size)
        return CGSize(
            width: clamp(offset.width, to: -limit.width...limit.width),
            height: clamp(offset.height, to: -limit.height...limit.height)
        )
    }
}

/// Pinch to zoom and drag to pan. Going past the limits springs back when you let go.
///
/// Double tap toggles the zoom. With Reduce Motion on, it settles without a spring.
struct PinchZoomView<Content: View>: View {
    @Binding var scale: CGFloat
    var minScale: CGFloat = 1
    var maxScale: CGFloat = 4
    @ViewBuilder var content: () -> Content

    @State private var pinch: CGFloat = 1
    @State private var offset = CGSize.zero
    @State private var drag = CGSize.zero
    @State private var size = CGSize.zero
    @GestureState private var isGesturing = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var settle: Animation {
        reduceMotion ? .easeOut(duration: 0.15) : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.25)
    }

    private var liveScale: CGFloat {
        PinchZoomViewMath.rubberBand(scale * pinch, in: minScale...maxScale)
    }

    private var liveOffset: CGSize {
        let limit = PinchZoomViewMath.maxOffset(scale: liveScale, size: size)
        return CGSize(
            width: PinchZoomViewMath.rubberBand(offset.width + drag.width, in: -limit.width...limit.width),
            height: PinchZoomViewMath.rubberBand(offset.height + drag.height, in: -limit.height...limit.height)
        )
    }

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .scaleEffect(liveScale)
            .offset(liveOffset)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .clipped()
            .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self) { $0.size } action: { newSize in
                size = newSize
                offset = PinchZoomViewMath.clampedOffset(offset, scale: scale, size: newSize)
            }
            .gesture(zoomAndPan)
            .onChange(of: isGesturing) { _, gesturing in
                if !gesturing { settleGesture() }
            }
            .onTapGesture(count: 2) { zoom(to: scale > minScale ? minScale : min(2, maxScale)) }
            .onChange(of: scale) { _, newScale in
                withAnimation(settle) { offset = PinchZoomViewMath.clampedOffset(offset, scale: newScale, size: size) }
            }
            .accessibilityValue("\(Int((scale * 100).rounded())) percent")
            .accessibilityZoomAction { action in
                zoom(to: scale + (action.direction == .zoomIn ? 0.5 : -0.5))
            }
    }

    private var zoomAndPan: some Gesture {
        MagnifyGesture()
            .simultaneously(with: DragGesture(minimumDistance: 4))
            .updating($isGesturing) { _, state, _ in state = true }
            .onChanged { value in
                if let magnification = value.first?.magnification { pinch = magnification }
                if let translation = value.second?.translation { drag = translation }
            }
            .onEnded { _ in settleGesture() }
    }

    /// Commits the live pinch and drag. A gesture the system cancels skips `onEnded`, so this
    /// also runs when `isGesturing` resets. Running it twice changes nothing.
    private func settleGesture() {
        let newScale = PinchZoomViewMath.clamp(scale * pinch, to: minScale...maxScale)
        let target = CGSize(width: offset.width + drag.width, height: offset.height + drag.height)
        withAnimation(settle) {
            scale = newScale
            pinch = 1
            drag = .zero
            offset = PinchZoomViewMath.clampedOffset(target, scale: newScale, size: size)
        }
    }

    private func zoom(to target: CGFloat) {
        withAnimation(settle) { scale = PinchZoomViewMath.clamp(target, to: minScale...maxScale) }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct PinchZoomViewDemo: View {
    @State private var scale: CGFloat = 1
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var zoomText: String {
        Double(scale).formatted(.number.precision(.fractionLength(1)))
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .bottom) {
            PinchZoomView(scale: $scale) { scene }
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            Text(zoomText)
                .font(.system(.title2, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .monospacedDigit()
                .contentTransition(.numericText())
                .padding(.horizontal, 24)
                .padding(.vertical, 12)
                .background(.ultraThinMaterial, in: .capsule)
                .padding(.bottom, 24)
                .accessibilityLabel("Zoom \(zoomText)")
        }
        .task {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            for target: CGFloat in [2.6, 1, 2.6, 1] {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.5))
                withAnimation(.spring(duration: 0.8, bounce: 0.2)) { scale = target }
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
            }
        }
    }

    private var scene: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .pink, .orange], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)

            Image(systemName: "sun.max.fill")
                .font(.system(.largeTitle))
                .imageScale(.large)
                .foregroundStyle(.yellow)
                .offset(y: -120)

            Image(systemName: "mountain.2.fill")
                .resizable()
                .scaledToFit()
                .foregroundStyle(.black.opacity(0.45))
                .padding(28)
                .offset(y: 90)
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("A mountain at sunset")
    }
}

#Preview {
    PinchZoomViewDemo()
}
```

## Glass Action Menu

A floating Liquid Glass button whose actions morph out of it.

Category: Glass. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Glass/GlassActionMenu/GlassActionMenu.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassActionItem: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let title: String
    let systemImage: String
    let action: () -> Void
}

/// A floating Liquid Glass button whose actions morph out of it.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the actions appear without morphing.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassActionMenu: View {
    private enum GlassID: Hashable, Sendable {
        case toggle
        case item(String)
    }

    let items: [GlassActionItem]

    @State private var isExpanded = false
    @Namespace private var namespace
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title2) private var buttonSize = 58.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var animation: Animation? {
        reduceMotion ? nil : .bouncy(duration: 0.5, extraBounce: 0.05)
    }

    var body: some View {
        // Known issue: iOS 27.2 reports the toggle's accessibility frame as the whole
        // stack when expanded. iOS 26.5 reports it correctly.
        GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 18) {
            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                if isExpanded {
                    ForEach(items) { item in
                        glassButton(id: .item(item.id), systemImage: item.systemImage, label: item.title) {
                            withAnimation(animation) { isExpanded = false }
                            item.action()
                        }
                    }
                }

                glassButton(
                    id: .toggle,
                    systemImage: "plus",
                    label: isExpanded ? "Close actions" : "Show actions",
                    rotation: isExpanded ? 45 : 0
                ) {
                    withAnimation(animation) { isExpanded.toggle() }
                }
            }
        }
        // The buttons only hold icons. Capping their growth keeps a tall stack on screen.
        .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.xxxLarge)
    }

    private func glassButton(
        id: GlassID,
        systemImage: String,
        label: String,
        rotation: Double = 0,
        action: @escaping () -> Void
    ) -> some View {
        Button(action: action) {
            Image(systemName: systemImage)
                .font(.title2.weight(.semibold))
                .rotationEffect(.degrees(rotation))
                .frame(width: buttonSize, height: buttonSize)
                .contentShape(.circle)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(label)
        .glassEffect(.regular.interactive(), in: .circle)
        .glassEffectID(id, in: namespace)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct GlassActionMenuDemo: View {
    @State private var lastAction = "Tap the button"

    private var items: [GlassActionItem] {
        [
            GlassActionItem(id: "share", title: "Share", systemImage: "square.and.arrow.up") { lastAction = "Share" },
            GlassActionItem(id: "favorite", title: "Favorite", systemImage: "star") { lastAction = "Favorite" },
            GlassActionItem(id: "delete", title: "Delete", systemImage: "trash") { lastAction = "Delete" },
        ]
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .bottomTrailing) {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink, .indigo], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            Text(lastAction)
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)

            GlassActionMenu(items: items)
                .padding(24)
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
#Preview {
    GlassActionMenuDemo()
}
```
