## Dots Pulse Loader

Three dots that pulse in sequence, as in a typing indicator.

Category: Loaders. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Loaders/DotsPulseLoader/DotsPulseLoader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Dots that pulse one after the other.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the dots stay still.
struct DotsPulseLoader: View {
    var color: Color = .indigo
    var dotCount: Int = 3
    var dotSize: CGFloat = 14

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Group {
            if reduceMotion {
                dots(activeIndex: nil)
            } else {
                PhaseAnimator(Array(0..<max(dotCount, 2))) { index in
                    dots(activeIndex: index)
                } animation: { _ in
                    .easeInOut(duration: 0.32)
                }
            }
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Loading")
    }

    private func dots(activeIndex: Int?) -> some View {
        HStack(spacing: dotSize * 0.6) {
            ForEach(0..<dotCount, id: \.self) { index in
                Circle()
                    .fill(color.gradient)
                    .frame(width: dotSize, height: dotSize)
                    .scaleEffect(scale(index: index, activeIndex: activeIndex))
                    .opacity(index == activeIndex || activeIndex == nil ? 1 : 0.4)
            }
        }
    }

    private func scale(index: Int, activeIndex: Int?) -> CGFloat {
        guard let activeIndex else { return 0.85 }
        return index == activeIndex ? 1.15 : 0.7
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct DotsPulseLoaderDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 48) {
            DotsPulseLoader(color: .indigo, dotSize: 44)

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) {
                Text("Did the package arrive?")
                    .font(.body)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    .padding(.horizontal, 16)
                    .padding(.vertical, 12)
                    .background(.blue.gradient, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 20))
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .trailing)

                DotsPulseLoader(color: .secondary, dotSize: 10)
                    .padding(.horizontal, 18)
                    .padding(.vertical, 16)
                    .background(Color(.secondarySystemBackground), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 20))
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 24)
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
    }
}

#Preview {
    DotsPulseLoaderDemo()
}
```

## Orbit Loader

A loading indicator with dots that orbit a glowing center.

Category: Loaders. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Loaders/OrbitLoader/OrbitLoader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Dots that orbit a glowing center, bunching up and spreading out as they go.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the dots stay still, evenly spaced around the center.
struct OrbitLoader: View {
    var color: Color = .indigo
    var dotCount: Int = 3
    var size: CGFloat = 64
    var period: TimeInterval = 1.6

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            let turns = reduceMotion ? 0 : context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate / period

            ZStack {
                Circle()
                    .stroke(color.opacity(0.2), lineWidth: size * 0.02)
                    .padding(size * 0.1)

                Circle()
                    .fill(color.gradient)
                    .frame(width: size * 0.26, height: size * 0.26)
                    .shadow(color: color.opacity(0.6), radius: size * 0.1)

                ForEach(0..<dotCount, id: \.self) { index in
                    Circle()
                        .fill(color.gradient)
                        .frame(width: size * 0.16, height: size * 0.16)
                        .offset(dotOffset(index: index, turns: turns))
                }
            }
            .frame(width: size, height: size)
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Loading")
    }

    private func dotOffset(index: Int, turns: Double) -> CGSize {
        let position = turns + Double(index) / Double(max(dotCount, 1))
        let angle = (position + 0.1 * sin(position * 2 * .pi)) * 2 * .pi
        let radius = size * 0.4
        return CGSize(width: cos(angle) * radius, height: sin(angle) * radius)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct OrbitLoaderDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .indigo.opacity(0.8)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 36) {
                OrbitLoader(color: .cyan, size: 240)

                VStack(spacing: 6) {
                    Text("Connecting")
                        .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)

                    Text("Looking for nearby devices")
                        .font(.body)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.75))
                }

                HStack(spacing: 32) {
                    OrbitLoader(color: .pink, dotCount: 2, size: 56)
                    OrbitLoader(color: .mint, dotCount: 4, size: 56, period: 2.4)
                    OrbitLoader(color: .orange, dotCount: 5, size: 56, period: 1.2)
                }
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    OrbitLoaderDemo()
}
```

## Skeleton Shimmer Modifier

A view modifier that turns any view into a shimmering redacted placeholder while it loads.

Category: Loaders. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Loaders/SkeletonShimmerModifier/SkeletonShimmerModifier.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

extension View {
    /// Shows this view as a shimmering placeholder while `active` is true.
    ///
    /// Apply it to the content inside a card, not to the card: the shimmer masks the
    /// view, so a shadow drawn outside its bounds would be cut off.
    func skeletonShimmer(active: Bool) -> some View {
        modifier(SkeletonShimmerModifier(active: active))
    }
}

/// Redacts its content and sweeps a band of light across the placeholders.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the placeholders stay still and slightly dimmed.
struct SkeletonShimmerModifier: ViewModifier {
    var active: Bool
    var duration: TimeInterval = 1.4

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .redacted(reason: active ? .placeholder : [])
            .mask {
                TimelineView(.animation(paused: !active || reduceMotion)) { context in
                    mask(at: context.date)
                }
            }
            .allowsHitTesting(!active)
            .accessibilityElement(children: active ? .ignore : .contain)
            .accessibilityLabel("Loading", isEnabled: active)
    }

    private func mask(at date: Date) -> LinearGradient {
        guard active else {
            return LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .black], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing)
        }
        guard !reduceMotion else {
            let dimmed = Color.black.opacity(0.6)
            return LinearGradient(colors: [dimmed, dimmed], startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing)
        }

        let progress = date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate.truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: duration) / duration
        let center = -0.5 + 2 * progress
        return LinearGradient(
            colors: [.black.opacity(0.35), .black, .black.opacity(0.35)],
            startPoint: UnitPoint(x: center - 0.5, y: 0.2),
            endPoint: UnitPoint(x: center + 0.5, y: 0.8)
        )
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow: Identifiable {
    let id = UUID()
    let name: String
    let message: String
    let time: String
    let color: Color
}

struct SkeletonShimmerModifierDemo: View {
    @State private var isLoading = true
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .headline) private var avatarSize = 46
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let rows = [
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Lucia Martin", message: "The photos from Sunday are up", time: "9:41", color: .pink),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Marco Rossi", message: "Can we move the call to four?", time: "9:12", color: .orange),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Aiko Tanaka", message: "Sent you the final invoice", time: "8:55", color: .teal),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Sam Porter", message: "Boarding now, see you tonight", time: "8:20", color: .indigo),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Nadia Haddad", message: "Loved the new onboarding", time: "Mon", color: .purple),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Tom Becker", message: "Tickets are booked for Friday", time: "Mon", color: .blue),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Elena Costa", message: "Recipe attached, enjoy it", time: "Sun", color: .green),
        SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow(name: "Ravi Patel", message: "The build is green again", time: "Sun", color: .mint),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        List {
            Section {
                ForEach(rows) { row in
                    rowContent(row)
                        .skeletonShimmer(active: isLoading)
                }
            } header: {
                Text("Messages")
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                    .foregroundStyle(.primary)
                    .textCase(nil)
                    .padding(.bottom, 8)
            }
        }
        .task {
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.2))
                withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .easeInOut(duration: 0.35)) {
                    isLoading.toggle()
                }
            }
        }
    }

    private func rowContent(_ row: SkeletonShimmerModifierDemoRow) -> some View {
        HStack(spacing: 12) {
            Circle()
                .fill(isLoading ? Color(.systemGray4) : row.color)
                .frame(width: avatarSize, height: avatarSize)
                .overlay {
                    Image(systemName: "person.fill")
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .opacity(isLoading ? 0 : 1)
                }
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                Text(row.name)
                    .font(.headline)

                Text(row.message)
                    .font(.subheadline)
                    .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
            }

            Spacer(minLength: 8)

            Text(row.time)
                .font(.caption)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
        .padding(.vertical, 4)
    }
}

#Preview {
    SkeletonShimmerModifierDemo()
}
```

## Symbol Breathe Loader

A loading indicator made of an SF Symbol that uses the breathe and rotate symbol effects.

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

import SwiftUI

enum SymbolBreatheLoaderEffect {
    case breathe
    case rotate
    case both
}

/// An SF Symbol that breathes, rotates or does both while something loads.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the symbol stays still.
struct SymbolBreatheLoader: View {
    var systemName: String = "sparkles"
    var effect: SymbolBreatheLoaderEffect = .breathe
    var color: Color = .indigo
    var font: Font = .largeTitle

    var body: some View {
        Image(systemName: systemName)
            .font(font)
            .symbolRenderingMode(.hierarchical)
            .foregroundStyle(color)
            .symbolEffect(.breathe, options: .repeat(.continuous), isActive: !reduceMotion && effect != .rotate)
            .symbolEffect(.rotate, options: .repeat(.continuous), isActive: !reduceMotion && effect != .breathe)
            .accessibilityLabel("Loading")
    }
}

                SymbolBreatheLoader(systemName: "arrow.trianglehead.2.clockwise", effect: .rotate, color: .blue)
                SymbolBreatheLoader(systemName: "heart.fill", color: .pink)
```

## Wave Bars Loader

A loading indicator with bars that rise and fall like an audio equalizer.

Category: Loaders. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Loaders/WaveBarsLoader/WaveBarsLoader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Bars that rise and fall like an equalizer.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the bars hold one uneven, still shape.
struct WaveBarsLoader: View {
    var colors: [Color] = [.blue, .cyan, .mint]
    var barCount: Int = 5
    var barWidth: CGFloat = 8
    var height: CGFloat = 44
    var speed: Double = 1

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            let time = reduceMotion ? 0 : context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate * speed

            HStack(alignment: .bottom, spacing: barWidth * 0.6) {
                ForEach(0..<barCount, id: \.self) { index in
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .bottom, endPoint: .top))
                        .frame(width: barWidth, height: barHeight(index: index, time: time))
                }
            }
            .frame(height: height, alignment: .bottom)
        }
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel("Loading")
    }

    /// Two sine waves at different speeds keep the bars from looking like a plain wave.
    private func barHeight(index: Int, time: Double) -> CGFloat {
        let position = Double(index)
        let level = 0.55 + 0.3 * sin(time * 5 + position * 0.8) + 0.15 * sin(time * 9 + position * 1.7)
        return max(barWidth, height * level)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct WaveBarsLoaderDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .blue.opacity(0.6)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 40) {
                WaveBarsLoader(barCount: 9, barWidth: 20, height: 220)

                VStack(spacing: 6) {
                    Text("Tuning in")
                        .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)

                    Text("Buffering your station")
                        .font(.body)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.75))
                }
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    WaveBarsLoaderDemo()
}
```

## Animatable Ring

A progress ring whose arc animates through the @Animatable macro.

Category: Modern. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Modern/AnimatableRing/AnimatableRing.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// An arc from `start` to `end` degrees. `@Animatable` writes its `animatableData`.
@available(iOS 26, *)
@Animatable
struct AnimatableRingArc: Shape {
    var start: Double
    var end: Double
    @AnimatableIgnored var clockwise = false

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        Path { path in
            path.addArc(
                center: CGPoint(x: rect.midX, y: rect.midY),
                radius: min(rect.width, rect.height) / 2,
                startAngle: .degrees(start - 90),
                endAngle: .degrees(end - 90),
                clockwise: clockwise
            )
        }
    }
}

/// A progress ring whose arc animates through the shape's own `animatableData`.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the ring jumps to the new value.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct AnimatableRing: View {
    let progress: Double
    var title: LocalizedStringKey = "Progress"
    var colors: [Color] = [.mint, .cyan, .blue, .mint]

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var lineWidth = 26.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var clamped: Double { min(max(progress, 0), 1) }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Circle()
                .stroke(.quaternary, lineWidth: lineWidth)

            AnimatableRingArc(start: 0, end: clamped * 360)
                .stroke(
                    AngularGradient(colors: colors, center: .center),
                    style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round)
                )

            Text(clamped, format: .percent.precision(.fractionLength(0)))
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .contentTransition(.numericText(value: clamped))
        }
        .padding(lineWidth / 2)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.8), value: clamped)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(title)
        .accessibilityValue(Text(clamped, format: .percent.precision(.fractionLength(0))))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct AnimatableRingDemo: View {
    @State private var progress = 0.72
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 24) {
            AnimatableRing(progress: progress, title: "Daily goal")
                .frame(width: 260, height: 260)

            Text("Daily goal")
                .font(.title2.bold())
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .task {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            let values = [0.28, 0.91, 0.55, 0.72]
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                for value in values where !Task.isCancelled {
                    try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
                    progress = value
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
#Preview {
    AnimatableRingDemo()
}
```

## Concentric Card

Nested cards whose corners stay concentric with ConcentricRectangle, however deep they sit.

Category: Modern. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Modern/ConcentricCard/ConcentricCard.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A card that publishes its corners, so `ConcentricCardSurface` views inside stay concentric.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct ConcentricCard<Background: ShapeStyle, Content: View>: View {
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat = 36
    var padding: CGFloat = 12
    let background: Background
    @ViewBuilder let content: () -> Content

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .padding(padding)
            .background(background, in: .rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
            .containerShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
    }
}

/// A surface whose corners follow the nearest container shape, however deep or inset it sits.
///
/// `minimumRadius` stops corners from turning square far from the container's edge.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct ConcentricCardSurface<Background: ShapeStyle, Content: View>: View {
    var padding: CGFloat = 12
    var minimumRadius: CGFloat = 8
    let background: Background
    @ViewBuilder let content: () -> Content

    var body: some View {
        content()
            .padding(padding)
            .background(background, in: ConcentricRectangle(corners: .concentric(minimum: .fixed(minimumRadius))))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct ConcentricCardDemo: View {
    @State private var inset: CGFloat = 8
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            ConcentricCard(cornerRadius: 56, padding: inset, background: Color.white.opacity(0.16)) {
                ConcentricCardSurface(padding: inset, background: Color.orange.gradient) {
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: inset) {
                        Label("Concentric", systemImage: "circle.circle")
                            .font(.title2.bold())
                            .foregroundStyle(.white)
                            .padding(16)
                            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 170, alignment: .bottomLeading)

                        ConcentricCardSurface(background: Color.white) {
                            Text("One shared center")
                                .font(.headline)
                                .foregroundStyle(.black)
                                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
        .task(id: reduceMotion) {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.3))
                guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
                withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.9)) { inset = inset == 8 ? 20 : 8 }
            }
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
#Preview {
    ConcentricCardDemo()
}
```

## Prominent Tab Bar

A tab view whose main action gets the system's prominent tab treatment.

Category: Modern. Minimum: iOS 27.0. Path: Components/Modern/ProminentTabBar/ProminentTabBar.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

@available(iOS 27, *)
struct ProminentTabBarItem<Value: Hashable>: Identifiable {
    let title: String
    let systemImage: String
    let value: Value

    var id: Value { value }
}

/// A tab view whose main action gets the system's prominent tab treatment.
@available(iOS 27, *)
struct ProminentTabBar<Value: Hashable, Content: View>: View {
    let tabs: [ProminentTabBarItem<Value>]
    let prominent: ProminentTabBarItem<Value>
    @Binding var selection: Value
    @ViewBuilder let content: (Value) -> Content

    var body: some View {
        TabView(selection: $selection) {
            ForEach(tabs) { tab in
                Tab(tab.title, systemImage: tab.systemImage, value: tab.value) {
                    content(tab.value)
                }
            }

            Tab(prominent.title, systemImage: prominent.systemImage, value: prominent.value, role: .prominent) {
                content(prominent.value)
            }
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 27, *)
struct ProminentTabBarDemo: View {
    private enum Screen: Hashable {
        case feed, explore, inbox, compose
    }

    @State private var selection = Screen.feed

    var body: some View {
        ProminentTabBar(
            tabs: [
                ProminentTabBarItem(title: "Feed", systemImage: "house.fill", value: .feed),
                ProminentTabBarItem(title: "Explore", systemImage: "safari.fill", value: .explore),
                ProminentTabBarItem(title: "Inbox", systemImage: "tray.fill", value: .inbox),
            ],
            prominent: ProminentTabBarItem(title: "Compose", systemImage: "plus", value: .compose),
            selection: $selection
        ) { screen in
            switch screen {
            case .feed: page("Good morning", icon: "sun.max.fill", colors: [.orange, .pink])
            case .explore: page("Find something new", icon: "binoculars.fill", colors: [.teal, .blue])
            case .inbox: page("All caught up", icon: "checkmark.seal.fill", colors: [.green, .mint])
            case .compose: page("Start writing", icon: "square.and.pencil", colors: [.purple, .indigo])
            }
        }
    }

    private func page(_ title: String, icon: String, colors: [Color]) -> some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                Image(systemName: icon)
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text(title)
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 27, *)
#Preview {
    ProminentTabBarDemo()
}
```

## Scroll Edge Header

A scroll view whose content dissolves under a custom header using the scroll edge effect.

Category: Modern. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Modern/ScrollEdgeHeader/ScrollEdgeHeader.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A scroll view whose content dissolves under a custom header.
///
/// The header sits in a safe area bar, which is what lets the scroll edge effect reach it.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct ScrollEdgeHeader<Header: View, Content: View>: View {
    var style: ScrollEdgeEffectStyle = .soft
    @ViewBuilder let header: () -> Header
    @ViewBuilder let content: () -> Content

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView(content: content)
            .scrollEdgeEffectStyle(style, for: .top)
            .safeAreaBar(edge: .top, content: header)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct ScrollEdgeHeaderDemo: View {
    @State private var isHard = false

    private let colors: [Color] = [.pink, .orange, .yellow, .green, .teal, .blue, .indigo, .purple]

    var body: some View {
        ScrollEdgeHeader(style: isHard ? .hard : .soft) {
            HStack {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
                    Text("Today")
                        .font(.largeTitle.bold())

                    Text(isHard ? "Hard edge" : "Soft edge")
                        .font(.subheadline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                }

                Spacer()

                Button("Change edge style", systemImage: "circle.lefthalf.filled") {
                    isHard.toggle()
                }
                .labelStyle(.iconOnly)
                .buttonStyle(.glass)
                .buttonBorderShape(.circle)
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 20)
            .padding(.bottom, 10)
        } content: {
            LazyVStack(spacing: 14) {
                ForEach(0..<30, id: \.self) { index in
                    Label("Story \(index + 1)", systemImage: "sparkles")
                        .font(.title3.bold())
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 120, alignment: .bottomLeading)
                        .padding(18)
                        .background(colors[index % colors.count].gradient, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))
                }
            }
            .padding(.horizontal, 20)
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
```

## Symbol Draw On

An SF Symbol that draws itself on and off, stroke by stroke.

Category: Modern. Minimum: iOS 26.0. Path: Components/Modern/SymbolDrawOn/SymbolDrawOn.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// An SF Symbol that draws itself on and off, stroke by stroke.
///
/// Only symbols with Draw annotations trace their strokes. Others fall back to a simpler
/// appearance. With Reduce Motion on, the symbol fades.
@available(iOS 26, *)
struct SymbolDrawOn: View {
    let systemName: String
    var isDrawn: Bool
    var label: LocalizedStringKey?

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Image(systemName: systemName)
            .symbolEffect(.drawOn.byLayer, isActive: !isDrawn)
            .symbolEffect(.drawOff.byLayer, isActive: !isDrawn)
            .symbolEffectsRemoved(reduceMotion)
            .opacity(reduceMotion && !isDrawn ? 0 : 1)
            .accessibilityHidden(label == nil)
            .accessibilityLabel(label ?? "")
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 26, *)
struct SymbolDrawOnDemo: View {
    @State private var isDrawn = true
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var cellSize = 104.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private let symbols = ["signature", "scribble", "wind", "sun.max", "cloud.rain", "checkmark.circle"]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .black], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem(.adaptive(minimum: cellSize))], spacing: 28) {
                ForEach(symbols, id: \.self) { symbol in
                    SymbolDrawOn(systemName: symbol, isDrawn: isDrawn)
                        .font(.largeTitle.weight(.medium))
                        .imageScale(.large)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .frame(height: cellSize)
                }
            }
            .padding(24)
        }
        .task {
            guard !reduceMotion else { return }
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(isDrawn ? 1.8 : 1.3))
                withAnimation { isDrawn.toggle() }
            }
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 26, *)
#Preview {
    SymbolDrawOnDemo()
}
```

## Toolbar Overflow Demo

A toolbar that ranks which actions survive when space runs out and keeps others in the overflow menu.

Category: Modern. Minimum: iOS 27.0. Path: Components/Modern/ToolbarOverflowDemo/ToolbarOverflowDemo.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

@available(iOS 27, *)
struct ToolbarOverflowDemoAction: Identifiable {
    let title: String
    let systemImage: String
    var priority: ToolbarItemVisibilityPriority = .automatic
    let perform: () -> Void

    var id: String { title }
}

/// A navigation screen that ranks which toolbar actions survive when space runs out.
///
/// `barActions` leave the bar lowest priority first. `overflowActions` always live in the menu.
@available(iOS 27, *)
struct ToolbarOverflowDemo<Content: View>: View {
    let title: String
    let barActions: [ToolbarOverflowDemoAction]
    let overflowActions: [ToolbarOverflowDemoAction]
    @ViewBuilder let content: () -> Content

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            content()
                .navigationTitle(title)
                .toolbarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)
                .toolbar {
                    ForEach(barActions) { action in
                        ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) {
                            button(for: action)
                        }
                        .visibilityPriority(action.priority)
                    }

                    ToolbarOverflowMenu {
                        ForEach(overflowActions, content: button(for:))
                    }
                }
        }
    }

    private func button(for action: ToolbarOverflowDemoAction) -> some View {
        Button(action.title, systemImage: action.systemImage, action: action.perform)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 27, *)
struct ToolbarOverflowDemoDemo: View {
    @State private var lastAction = "Pick an action"

    private func action(
        _ title: String,
        _ systemImage: String,
        _ priority: ToolbarItemVisibilityPriority = .automatic
    ) -> ToolbarOverflowDemoAction {
        ToolbarOverflowDemoAction(title: title, systemImage: systemImage, priority: priority) { lastAction = title }
    }

    var body: some View {
        ToolbarOverflowDemo(
            title: "Draft",
            barActions: [
                action("Share", "square.and.arrow.up", .high),
                action("Flag", "flag", .low),
                action("Comment", "text.bubble"),
                action("Tag", "tag"),
                action("Archive", "archivebox", .low),
                action("Bookmark", "bookmark", .high),
                action("Pin", "pin", .high),
            ],
            overflowActions: [
                action("Duplicate", "plus.square.on.square"),
                action("Export as PDF", "doc.richtext"),
                action("Print", "printer"),
            ]
        ) {
            ZStack {
                LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .purple, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                    .ignoresSafeArea()

                Text(lastAction)
                    .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    .contentTransition(.opacity)
                    .animation(.easeInOut, value: lastAction)
            }
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 27, *)
#Preview {
    ToolbarOverflowDemoDemo()
}
```

## Animated Tab Bar

A custom tab bar with a sliding indicator and icons that bounce on selection.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/AnimatedTabBar/AnimatedTabBar.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

struct AnimatedTabBarItem<Value: Hashable>: Identifiable {
    let value: Value
    let title: String
    let systemImage: String

    var id: Value { value }
}

/// A custom tab bar whose indicator slides to the selected tab while its icon bounces.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the indicator jumps and the icons stay still.
struct AnimatedTabBar<Value: Hashable>: View {
    let items: [AnimatedTabBarItem<Value>]
    @Binding var selection: Value
    var tint: Color = .indigo

    @State private var bounces: [Value: Int] = [:]
    @Namespace private var indicator
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title3) private var iconHeight = 26.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: 4) {
            ForEach(items) { item in
                tabButton(item)
            }
        }
        .padding(6)
        .background(.regularMaterial, in: .capsule)
        .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.15), radius: 16, y: 8)
        .symbolEffectsRemoved(reduceMotion)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3), value: selection)
        .onChange(of: selection) { _, newValue in
            bounces[newValue, default: 0] += 1
        }
    }

    private func tabButton(_ item: AnimatedTabBarItem<Value>) -> some View {
        let isSelected = item.value == selection

        return Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.3)) {
                selection = item.value
            }
        } label: {
            VStack(spacing: 2) {
                Image(systemName: item.systemImage)
                    .font(.title3.weight(.semibold))
                    .symbolEffect(.bounce, value: bounces[item.value, default: 0])
                    .frame(height: iconHeight)

                Text(item.title)
                    .font(.caption2.weight(.semibold))
                    .lineLimit(1)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(isSelected ? tint : Color.secondary)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .padding(.vertical, 8)
            .background {
                if isSelected {
                    Capsule()
                        .fill(tint.opacity(0.18))
                        .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "indicator", in: indicator)
                }
            }
            .contentShape(.capsule)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(item.title)
        .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct AnimatedTabBarDemo: View {
    private enum Destination: Hashable {
        case home, search, saved, profile
    }

    private let items: [AnimatedTabBarItem<Destination>] = [
        AnimatedTabBarItem(value: .home, title: "Home", systemImage: "house.fill"),
        AnimatedTabBarItem(value: .search, title: "Search", systemImage: "magnifyingglass"),
        AnimatedTabBarItem(value: .saved, title: "Saved", systemImage: "bookmark.fill"),
        AnimatedTabBarItem(value: .profile, title: "Profile", systemImage: "person.fill"),
    ]

    @State private var selection = Destination.home

    private var page: (headline: String, colors: [Color]) {
        switch selection {
        case .home: ("Your day at a glance", [.indigo, .purple])
        case .search: ("Find anything", [.teal, .blue])
        case .saved: ("Kept for later", [.orange, .pink])
        case .profile: ("All about you", [.green, .teal])
        }
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .bottom) {
            LinearGradient(colors: page.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()
                .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.4), value: selection)

            Text(page.headline)
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                .padding(32)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)

            AnimatedTabBar(items: items, selection: $selection)
                .padding(.horizontal, 20)
                .padding(.bottom, 8)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    AnimatedTabBarDemo()
}
```

## Bottom Drawer

A draggable bottom drawer that snaps to detents, built as a custom overlay.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/BottomDrawer/BottomDrawer.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

enum BottomDrawerSnapping {
    /// The stop closest to where a drag would come to rest. A drag upwards has a negative `predictedDrag`.
    static func stop(from current: CGFloat, predictedDrag: CGFloat, stops: [CGFloat]) -> CGFloat {
        let projected = current - predictedDrag
        return stops.min { abs($0 - projected) < abs($1 - projected) } ?? current
    }

    /// The stop `step` places away from `current`, held at the ends. With no stops it keeps `current`.
    static func stop(from current: CGFloat, step: Int, stops: [CGFloat]) -> CGFloat {
        let sorted = stops.sorted()
        guard !sorted.isEmpty else { return current }
        let index = sorted.firstIndex(of: current) ?? 0
        return sorted[min(max(index + step, 0), sorted.count - 1)]
    }

    /// Keeps the drawer between its lowest and highest stop while it is dragged.
    static func clamped(_ value: CGFloat, stops: [CGFloat]) -> CGFloat {
        guard let lowest = stops.min(), let highest = stops.max() else { return value }
        return min(max(value, lowest), highest)
    }
}

/// A drawer that rests on detents, given as fractions of the available height.
///
/// Place it above your content in a `ZStack`. The whole drawer is draggable, so keep scrolling
/// content out of it. VoiceOver adjusts the handle. With Reduce Motion on, the drawer snaps without a spring.
struct BottomDrawer<Content: View>: View {
    @Binding var detent: CGFloat
    var detents: [CGFloat] = [0.16, 0.5, 0.88]
    @ViewBuilder var content: Content

    @State private var dragTranslation: CGFloat = 0
    @GestureState private var isDragging = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var animation: Animation? {
        reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.2)
    }

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            let total = max(proxy.size.height, 1)
            let visible = BottomDrawerSnapping.clamped(detent - dragTranslation / total, stops: detents)

            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                handle
                content
                Spacer(minLength: 0)
            }
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .frame(height: (detents.max() ?? 1) * total, alignment: .top)
            .background(.regularMaterial, in: UnevenRoundedRectangle(topLeadingRadius: 28, topTrailingRadius: 28))
            .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.18), radius: 18, y: -4)
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .offset(y: total * (1 - visible))
            .gesture(dragGesture(total: total))
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea(edges: .bottom)
        .onChange(of: isDragging) { _, dragging in
            if !dragging { withAnimation(animation) { dragTranslation = 0 } }
        }
    }

    private var handle: some View {
        Capsule()
            .fill(.secondary)
            .frame(width: 40, height: 5)
            .padding(.vertical, 12)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .contentShape(.rect)
            .accessibilityElement()
            .accessibilityLabel("Drawer")
            .accessibilityValue("Position \(sortedIndex + 1) of \(detents.count)")
            .accessibilityAdjustableAction { direction in
                switch direction {
                case .increment: moveDetent(by: 1)
                case .decrement: moveDetent(by: -1)
                @unknown default: break
                }
            }
    }

    private var sortedDetents: [CGFloat] { detents.sorted() }
    private var sortedIndex: Int { sortedDetents.firstIndex(of: detent) ?? 0 }

    private func moveDetent(by step: Int) {
        withAnimation(animation) { detent = BottomDrawerSnapping.stop(from: detent, step: step, stops: detents) }
    }

    private func dragGesture(total: CGFloat) -> some Gesture {
        DragGesture()
            .updating($isDragging) { _, state, _ in state = true }
            .onChanged { dragTranslation = $0.translation.height }
            .onEnded { value in
                let target = BottomDrawerSnapping.stop(
                    from: detent,
                    predictedDrag: value.predictedEndTranslation.height / total,
                    stops: detents
                )
                withAnimation(animation) {
                    detent = target
                    dragTranslation = 0
                }
            }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BottomDrawerDemo: View {
    @State private var detent: CGFloat = 0.16

    private let places = [
        ("Harbor Coffee", "cup.and.saucer.fill", Color.brown),
        ("City Library", "books.vertical.fill", Color.indigo),
        ("Riverside Park", "leaf.fill", Color.green),
        ("Old Town Bakery", "birthday.cake.fill", Color.pink),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.teal, .cyan, .mint], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            Image(systemName: "mappin.and.ellipse")
                .font(.largeTitle)
                .imageScale(.large)
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .shadow(radius: 6)
                .offset(y: -180)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            BottomDrawer(detent: $detent) {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 18) {
                    Text("Nearby")
                        .font(.title2.bold())

                    ForEach(places, id: \.0) { name, symbol, color in
                        Label {
                            Text(name).font(.headline)
                        } icon: {
                            Image(systemName: symbol).foregroundStyle(color.gradient)
                        }
                    }
                }
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                .padding(.horizontal, 24)
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    BottomDrawerDemo()
}
```

## Page Dots Indicator

Page dots where the current one stretches into a capsule, following a paged TabView or scroll.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/PageDotsIndicator/PageDotsIndicator.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Page dots where the current one stretches into a capsule. Bind `current` to a paged `TabView` or a scroll position.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the capsule changes without animating.
struct PageDotsIndicator: View {
    let count: Int
    let current: Int
    var tint: Color = .primary

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .caption) private var dotSize = 8.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        HStack(spacing: dotSize) {
            ForEach(0..<max(count, 0), id: \.self) { index in
                Capsule()
                    .fill(tint.opacity(index == current ? 1 : 0.25))
                    .frame(width: index == current ? dotSize * 3 : dotSize, height: dotSize)
            }
        }
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.35, bounce: 0.3), value: current)
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel("Page")
        .accessibilityValue("\(current + 1) of \(count)")
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct PageDotsIndicatorDemo: View {
    private let pages: [(title: String, symbol: String, colors: [Color])] = [
        ("Plan your trip", "map.fill", [.blue, .indigo]),
        ("Book in seconds", "ticket.fill", [.pink, .orange]),
        ("Pack with a list", "suitcase.fill", [.teal, .green]),
        ("Share the memories", "camera.fill", [.purple, .pink]),
    ]

    @State private var page = 0

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 24) {
            TabView(selection: $page) {
                ForEach(pages.indices, id: \.self) { index in
                    VStack(spacing: 24) {
                        Image(systemName: pages[index].symbol)
                            .font(.largeTitle)
                            .imageScale(.large)
                            .accessibilityHidden(true)

                        Text(pages[index].title)
                            .font(.title.bold())
                    }
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
                    .background(
                        LinearGradient(colors: pages[index].colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing),
                        in: .rect(cornerRadius: 32)
                    )
                    .padding(.horizontal, 20)
                    .tag(index)
                }
            }
            .tabViewStyle(.page(indexDisplayMode: .never))

            PageDotsIndicator(count: pages.count, current: page)
                .padding(.bottom, 16)
        }
    }
}
```

## Scroll To Top Button

A floating button that appears after scrolling down and returns the scroll view to the top.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/ScrollToTopButton/ScrollToTopButton.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A scroll view that shows a floating button after scrolling down, which returns to the top.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the button fades and the view jumps to the top.
struct ScrollToTopButton<Content: View>: View {
    var threshold: CGFloat = 320
    var tint: Color = .indigo
    @ViewBuilder var content: Content

    @State private var position = ScrollPosition(edge: .top)
    @State private var isVisible = false
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title3) private var buttonSize = 52.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            content
        }
        .scrollPosition($position)
        .onScrollGeometryChange(for: Bool.self) { geometry in
            geometry.contentOffset.y + geometry.contentInsets.top > threshold
        } action: { _, isPastThreshold in
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? .easeInOut(duration: 0.2) : .spring(duration: 0.4, bounce: 0.35)) {
                isVisible = isPastThreshold
            }
        }
        .overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing) {
            if isVisible {
                button
                    .padding(20)
                    .transition(reduceMotion ? .opacity : .scale(scale: 0.4).combined(with: .opacity))
            }
        }
    }

    private var button: some View {
        Button {
            withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.5)) {
                position.scrollTo(edge: .top)
            }
        } label: {
            Image(systemName: "arrow.up")
                .font(.title3.bold())
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .frame(width: buttonSize, height: buttonSize)
                .background(tint.gradient, in: .circle)
                .shadow(color: .black.opacity(0.25), radius: 10, y: 5)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel("Back to top")
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ScrollToTopButtonDemo: View {
    private let colors: [Color] = [.indigo, .blue, .teal, .green, .orange, .pink]

    var body: some View {
        ScrollToTopButton {
            LazyVStack(spacing: 14) {
                ForEach(0..<30, id: \.self) { index in
                    HStack(spacing: 14) {
                        Image(systemName: "photo.fill")
                            .font(.title2)
                            .foregroundStyle(.white)
                            .frame(width: 60, height: 60)
                            .background(colors[index % colors.count].gradient, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 14))
                            .accessibilityHidden(true)

                        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
                            Text("Story \(index + 1)")
                                .font(.headline)
                            Text("A short description of this story")
                                .font(.subheadline)
                                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                        }

                        Spacer(minLength: 0)
                    }
                    .padding(12)
                    .background(.regularMaterial, in: .rect(cornerRadius: 18))
                }
            }
            .padding(16)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ScrollToTopButtonDemo()
}
```

## Side Drawer

A side menu that slides in and pushes the content away, with drag to open and close.

Category: Navigation. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Navigation/SideDrawer/SideDrawer.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A side menu that pushes the content away. Drag sideways or tap the content to close it.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the menu opens and closes without sliding.
struct SideDrawer<MenuContent: View, Content: View>: View {
    @Binding var isOpen: Bool
    var menuWidth: CGFloat = 280
    @ViewBuilder var menu: MenuContent
    @ViewBuilder var content: Content

    @State private var dragTranslation: CGFloat = 0
    @GestureState private var isDragging = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var animation: Animation? {
        reduceMotion ? nil : .spring(duration: 0.45, bounce: 0.15)
    }

    private var pushOffset: CGFloat {
        min(max((isOpen ? menuWidth : 0) + dragTranslation, 0), menuWidth)
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .leading) {
            menu
                .frame(width: menuWidth)
                .frame(maxHeight: .infinity)
                .offset(x: pushOffset - menuWidth)
                .accessibilityHidden(!isOpen)

            content
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
                .accessibilityHidden(isOpen)
                .overlay {
                    if isOpen {
                        Button {
                            isOpen = false
                        } label: {
                            Color.clear.contentShape(.rect)
                        }
                        .buttonStyle(.plain)
                        .accessibilityLabel("Close menu")
                    }
                }
                .shadow(color: .black.opacity(pushOffset > 0 ? 0.3 : 0), radius: 20)
                .offset(x: pushOffset)
        }
        .gesture(dragGesture)
        .animation(animation, value: isOpen)
        .onChange(of: isDragging) { _, dragging in
            if !dragging { withAnimation(animation) { dragTranslation = 0 } }
        }
    }

    private var dragGesture: some Gesture {
        DragGesture(minimumDistance: 20)
            .updating($isDragging) { _, state, _ in state = true }
            .onChanged { dragTranslation = $0.translation.width }
            .onEnded { value in
                let projected = (isOpen ? menuWidth : 0) + value.predictedEndTranslation.width
                withAnimation(animation) {
                    isOpen = projected > menuWidth / 2
                    dragTranslation = 0
                }
            }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SideDrawerDemo: View {
    private let destinations = [
        ("Inbox", "tray.fill"),
        ("Starred", "star.fill"),
        ("Archive", "archivebox.fill"),
        ("Settings", "gearshape.fill"),
    ]

    @State private var isOpen = false
    @State private var current = "tray.fill"

    var body: some View {
        SideDrawer(isOpen: $isOpen) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 26) {
                Text("Workspace")
                    .font(.title2.bold())
                    .padding(.bottom, 8)

                ForEach(destinations, id: \.0) { name, symbol in
                    Button {
                        current = symbol
                        isOpen = false
                    } label: {
                        Label(name, systemImage: symbol)
                            .font(.headline)
                    }
                }

                Spacer()
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .padding(.top, 40)
            .padding(.horizontal, 28)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
        } content: {
            ZStack(alignment: .topLeading) {
                LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                    .ignoresSafeArea()

                Image(systemName: current)
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .foregroundStyle(.white)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Button {
                    isOpen = true
                } label: {
                    Image(systemName: "line.3.horizontal")
                        .font(.title2.bold())
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .padding(14)
                        .background(.white.opacity(0.2), in: .circle)
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
                .accessibilityLabel("Menu")
                .padding(20)
            }
        }
        .background(LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .black], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom).ignoresSafeArea())
    }
}

    SideDrawerDemo()
}
```

## Circular Progress Ring

An animated gradient ring that shows progress with a percentage in the middle.

Category: Progress. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Progress/CircularProgressRing/CircularProgressRing.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// The clamping and the text of the ring, apart from the view so they can be tested.
enum CircularProgressRingMath {
    static func clamped(_ value: Double) -> Double {
        value.isNaN ? 0 : min(max(value, 0), 1)
    }

    /// Only a finished ring reads 100: 99.6% rounds down to 99.
    static func wholePercent(_ value: Double) -> Int {
        let fraction = clamped(value)
        let percent = Int((fraction * 100).rounded())
        return percent == 100 && fraction < 1 ? 99 : percent
    }

    static func percentText(_ value: Double, locale: Locale = .autoupdatingCurrent) -> String {
        wholePercent(value).formatted(.percent.locale(locale))
    }
}

/// An animated ring with a gradient and the percentage in the middle. Give it a frame to size it.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the ring and the number change without animating.
struct CircularProgressRing: View {
    var progress: Double
    var colors: [Color] = [.cyan, .blue, .purple]
    var lineWidth: CGFloat = 18
    var font: Font = .system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold)
    var label: LocalizedStringKey = "Progress"

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var value: Double { CircularProgressRingMath.clamped(progress) }
    private var percentText: String { CircularProgressRingMath.percentText(progress) }
    private var strokeStyle: StrokeStyle { StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round) }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Circle()
                .stroke(.quaternary, lineWidth: lineWidth)

            ZStack {
                Circle()
                    .trim(from: 0, to: value)
                    .stroke(AngularGradient(colors: colors, center: .center), style: strokeStyle)

                // The round cap at the start falls on the gradient's seam, so paint it with the first color.
                Circle()
                    .trim(from: 0, to: value > 0 ? 0.001 : 0)
                    .stroke(colors.first ?? .blue, style: strokeStyle)
            }
            .rotationEffect(.degrees(-90))

            Text(percentText)
                .font(font)
                .monospacedDigit()
                .contentTransition(.numericText(value: value))
                .minimumScaleFactor(0.4)
                .lineLimit(1)
                .padding(lineWidth + 4)
        }
        .padding(lineWidth / 2)
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.7), value: value)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(label)
        .accessibilityValue(percentText)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CircularProgressRingDemo: View {
    @State private var progress = 0.0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var percentSize = 60

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 40) {
            Text("Uploading photos")
                .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

            CircularProgressRing(
                progress: progress,
                lineWidth: 26,
                font: .system(size: percentSize, weight: .bold, design: .rounded),
                label: "Upload"
            )
            .frame(width: 280)

            HStack(spacing: 28) {
                CircularProgressRing(progress: 0.32, colors: [.pink, .orange], lineWidth: 8, font: .headline, label: "Move")
                CircularProgressRing(progress: 0.68, colors: [.green, .mint], lineWidth: 8, font: .headline, label: "Exercise")
                CircularProgressRing(progress: 0.91, colors: [.teal, .blue], lineWidth: 8, font: .headline, label: "Stand")
            }
            .frame(height: 88)
        }
        .padding(24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .task {
            let values = [0.25, 0.6, 0.85, 1, 0]
            var index = 0
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                progress = values[index]
                index = (index + 1) % values.count
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.9))
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    CircularProgressRingDemo()
}
```

## Countdown Ring

A ring that empties and a number that counts down to a date.

Category: Progress. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Progress/CountdownRing/CountdownRing.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// The time math of the ring, apart from the view so it can be tested.
enum CountdownRingMath {
    static func remaining(now: Date, endDate: Date, duration: TimeInterval) -> TimeInterval {
        min(max(endDate.timeIntervalSince(now), 0), max(duration, 0))
    }

    static func fraction(remaining: TimeInterval, duration: TimeInterval) -> Double {
        guard duration > 0 else { return 0 }
        return min(max(remaining / duration, 0), 1)
    }

    /// Rounds up, so the number only reaches 0 when the time is really over.
    static func wholeSeconds(remaining: TimeInterval) -> Int {
        Int(max(remaining, 0).rounded(.up))
    }

    /// `45` below a minute, `1:05` from then on.
    static func text(seconds: Int, locale: Locale = .autoupdatingCurrent) -> String {
        guard seconds >= 60 else {
            return seconds.formatted(.number.locale(locale))
        }
        return Duration.seconds(seconds).formatted(.time(pattern: .minuteSecond).locale(locale))
    }
}

/// A ring that empties and a number that counts down to `endDate`. Give it a frame to size it.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the ring moves once per second instead of continuously.
struct CountdownRing: View {
    var endDate: Date
    var duration: TimeInterval
    var colors: [Color] = [.orange, .pink]
    var lineWidth: CGFloat = 18
    var font: Font = .system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold)
    var onFinish: (() -> Void)? = nil

    @State private var isFinished = false
    @State private var notifiedEndDate: Date?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: reduceMotion ? 0.25 : 1.0 / 30.0, paused: isFinished)) { context in
            let remaining = CountdownRingMath.remaining(
                now: isFinished ? endDate : context.date,
                endDate: endDate,
                duration: duration
            )
            let seconds = CountdownRingMath.wholeSeconds(remaining: remaining)
            let fraction = CountdownRingMath.fraction(
                remaining: reduceMotion ? TimeInterval(seconds) : remaining,
                duration: duration
            )

            ZStack {
                Circle()
                    .stroke(.quaternary, lineWidth: lineWidth)

                Circle()
                    .trim(from: 0, to: fraction)
                    .stroke(
                        LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom),
                        style: StrokeStyle(lineWidth: lineWidth, lineCap: .round)
                    )
                    .rotationEffect(.degrees(-90))

                Text(CountdownRingMath.text(seconds: seconds))
                    .font(font)
                    .monospacedDigit()
                    .contentTransition(.numericText(value: Double(seconds)))
                    .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .snappy, value: seconds)
                    .minimumScaleFactor(0.4)
                    .lineLimit(1)
                    .padding(lineWidth + 4)
            }
            .padding(lineWidth / 2)
            .accessibilityElement()
            .accessibilityLabel("Time remaining")
            .accessibilityValue("\(seconds) seconds")
        }
        .aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit)
        .task(id: endDate) {
            isFinished = false
            let delay = endDate.timeIntervalSinceNow
            if delay > 0 {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(delay))
            }
            guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }
            isFinished = true
            guard notifiedEndDate != endDate else { return }
            notifiedEndDate = endDate
            onFinish?()
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CountdownRingDemo: View {
    @State private var endDate = Date.now.addingTimeInterval(3)
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var numberSize = 96

    private let duration: TimeInterval = 3

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 36) {
            Text("Get ready")
                .font(.system(.title, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

            CountdownRing(
                endDate: endDate,
                duration: duration,
                lineWidth: 26,
                font: .system(size: numberSize, weight: .bold, design: .rounded)
            )
            .frame(width: 280)

            Text("Your next set starts soon")
                .font(.body)
                .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
        }
        .padding(24)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .task {
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(duration + 0.8))
                endDate = Date.now.addingTimeInterval(duration)
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    CountdownRingDemo()
}
```

## Gradient Progress Bar

A rounded progress bar with a gradient fill that glows more strongly as it advances.

Category: Progress. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Progress/GradientProgressBar/GradientProgressBar.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A rounded bar whose gradient fill glows more strongly as it advances.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the fill changes without animating.
struct GradientProgressBar: View {
    var progress: Double
    var colors: [Color] = [.cyan, .blue, .purple]
    var height: CGFloat = 12
    var label: LocalizedStringKey = "Progress"

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var value: Double {
        progress.isNaN ? 0 : min(max(progress, 0), 1)
    }

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            ZStack(alignment: .leading) {
                Capsule()
                    .fill(.quaternary)

                Capsule()
                    .fill(LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .leading, endPoint: .trailing))
                    .frame(width: value > 0 ? max(height, proxy.size.width * value) : 0)
                    .shadow(color: (colors.last ?? .blue).opacity(0.25 + 0.55 * value), radius: 3 + 12 * value)
            }
        }
        .frame(height: height)
        .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.6), value: value)
        .accessibilityElement()
        .accessibilityLabel(label)
        .accessibilityValue(Text(value, format: .percent.precision(.fractionLength(0))))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct GradientProgressBarDemo: View {
    @State private var progress = 0.08

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .indigo.opacity(0.6)], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 44) {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 18) {
                    Text("Downloading")
                        .font(.headline)
                        .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.75))

                    Text(progress, format: .percent.precision(.fractionLength(0)))
                        .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                        .monospacedDigit()
                        .foregroundStyle(.white)
                        .contentTransition(.numericText(value: progress))

                    GradientProgressBar(progress: progress, height: 22, label: "Download")
                }

                row("Maps", value: progress * 0.7, colors: [.mint, .green])
                row("Music", value: progress * 0.45, colors: [.orange, .pink])
            }
            .padding(28)
        }
        .environment(\.colorScheme, .dark)
        .task {
            let values = [0.08, 0.34, 0.62, 1, 0.08]
            var index = 0
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.9))
                index = (index + 1) % values.count
                withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.3)) { progress = values[index] }
            }
        }
    }

    private func row(_ title: LocalizedStringKey, value: Double, colors: [Color]) -> some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 10) {
            Text(title)
                .font(.subheadline)
                .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.75))

            GradientProgressBar(progress: value, colors: colors, label: title)
        }
    }
}

}
```
