## Text Blur Reveal

Text that appears line by line, coming into focus as it slides up, drawn by a custom TextRenderer.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/TextBlurReveal/TextBlurReveal.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Reveals text line by line: each line fades in, comes into focus and slides up.
///
/// Animate `progress` from 0 to 1 with `withAnimation`. With Reduce Motion on, the text is shown in full.
struct TextBlurReveal: View {
    let text: String
    var progress: Double = 1

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title) private var blurRadius = 12.0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title) private var rise = 18.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        Text(text)
            .textRenderer(TextBlurRevealRenderer(
                progress: reduceMotion ? 1 : progress,
                blurRadius: blurRadius,
                rise: rise
            ))
    }
}

struct TextBlurRevealRenderer: TextRenderer {
    var progress: Double
    var blurRadius: Double
    var rise: Double

    /// How much of each line's animation overlaps with the next one.
    private let overlap = 0.55

    var animatableData: Double {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    /// Room for the blur and the slide, which draw outside the text's own frame.
    var displayPadding: EdgeInsets {
        let margin = blurRadius * 2
        return EdgeInsets(top: margin, leading: margin, bottom: margin + rise, trailing: margin)
    }

    func draw(layout: Text.Layout, in context: inout GraphicsContext) {
        for (index, line) in layout.enumerated() {
            let reveal = lineProgress(index: index, count: layout.count)

            var lineContext = context
            lineContext.opacity = reveal
            lineContext.addFilter(.blur(radius: (1 - reveal) * blurRadius))
            lineContext.translateBy(x: 0, y: (1 - reveal) * rise)
            lineContext.draw(line)
        }
    }

    private func lineProgress(index: Int, count: Int) -> Double {
        let step = 1 - overlap
        let lineDuration = 1 / (Double(count - 1) * step + 1)
        let lineStart = Double(index) * step * lineDuration
        return min(max((progress - lineStart) / lineDuration, 0), 1)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct TextBlurRevealDemo: View {
    @State private var progress = 0.0

    private let poem = """
    The morning arrives
    without asking anyone,
    one quiet line
    after another,
    until the page is full.
    """

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .black], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            TextBlurReveal(text: poem, progress: progress)
                .font(.system(.title, design: .serif, weight: .medium))
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                .lineSpacing(10)
                .padding(32)
        }
        .task {
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 2.2)) { progress = 1 }
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(3.4))
                progress = 0
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(0.2))
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    TextBlurRevealDemo()
}
```

## Typewriter Text

Text that types itself one character at a time, followed by a blinking cursor.

Category: Text. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Text/TypewriterText/TypewriterText.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Types its text one character at a time, followed by a blinking cursor.
///
/// It restarts when `text` changes. With Reduce Motion on, the text appears in full with no cursor.
struct TypewriterText: View {
    let text: String
    var charactersPerSecond: Double = 20
    var cursorColor: Color = .accentColor

    @State private var started: (text: String, date: Date)?
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        TimelineView(.animation(minimumInterval: 1.0 / 30.0, paused: reduceMotion)) { context in
            Text(typed(at: context.date))
        }
        .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
        .accessibilityLabel(text)
        .task(id: text) { started = (text, .now) }
    }

    /// The characters not typed yet stay in the string as clear text, so lines wrap once and never jump.
    private func typed(at date: Date) -> AttributedString {
        guard !reduceMotion else { return AttributedString(text) }

        let elapsed = started.flatMap { $0.text == text ? date.timeIntervalSince($0.date) : nil } ?? 0
        let count = TypewriterTextProgress.visibleCount(
            elapsed: elapsed,
            charactersPerSecond: charactersPerSecond,
            total: text.count
        )
        let isTyping = count < text.count

        var cursor = AttributedString("|")
        cursor.foregroundColor = isTyping || Int(elapsed * 2).isMultiple(of: 2) ? cursorColor : .clear

        var remaining = AttributedString(String(text.dropFirst(count)))
        remaining.foregroundColor = .clear

        return AttributedString(String(text.prefix(count))) + cursor + remaining
    }
}

enum TypewriterTextProgress {
    /// How many characters are visible after `elapsed` seconds, from 0 to `total`.
    static func visibleCount(elapsed: TimeInterval, charactersPerSecond: Double, total: Int) -> Int {
        guard total > 0 else { return 0 }
        guard charactersPerSecond > 0 else { return total }

        let typed = (elapsed * charactersPerSecond).rounded(.down)
        guard typed > 0 else { return 0 }
        return typed >= Double(total) ? total : Int(typed)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct TypewriterTextDemo: View {
    @State private var index = 0

    private let lines = [
        "$ swift build\nCompiling your ideas...",
        "$ swift test\nAll tests passed, no bugs today.",
        "$ git push\nShipped before lunch.",
    ]

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color.black.ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
                HStack(spacing: 8) {
                    ForEach([Color.red, .yellow, .green], id: \.self) { color in
                        Circle().fill(color).frame(width: 12, height: 12)
                    }
                }
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

                TypewriterText(text: lines[index], cursorColor: .green)
                    .font(.system(.title2, design: .monospaced, weight: .medium))
                    .foregroundStyle(.green)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: 160, alignment: .topLeading)
            }
            .padding(24)
            .background(.white.opacity(0.08), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 20))
            .padding(20)
        }
        .task {
            while !Task.isCancelled {
                try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(3.2))
                index = (index + 1) % lines.count
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    TypewriterTextDemo()
}
```

## Blur Fade Transition

A custom transition that combines blur, fade and scale, available as .blurFade.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/BlurFadeTransition/BlurFadeTransition.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A transition that blurs, fades and scales a view. Use it as `.transition(.blurFade)`.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the view only fades.
struct BlurFadeTransition: Transition {
    var radius: CGFloat = 18
    var scale: CGFloat = 0.9

    func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.modifier(BlurFadeEffect(radius: radius, scale: scale, isIdentity: phase.isIdentity))
    }
}

extension Transition where Self == BlurFadeTransition {
    static var blurFade: BlurFadeTransition { BlurFadeTransition() }

    static func blurFade(radius: CGFloat, scale: CGFloat = 0.9) -> BlurFadeTransition {
        BlurFadeTransition(radius: radius, scale: scale)
    }
}

// The effect lives in a view modifier so it can read the environment.
private struct BlurFadeEffect: ViewModifier {
    let radius: CGFloat
    let scale: CGFloat
    let isIdentity: Bool

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .blur(radius: isIdentity || reduceMotion ? 0 : radius)
            .scaleEffect(isIdentity || reduceMotion ? 1 : scale)
            .opacity(isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct BlurFadeTransitionDemo: View {
    @State private var isShown = true

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.black, .indigo], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            if isShown {
                VStack(spacing: 14) {
                    Image(systemName: "moon.stars.fill")
                        .font(.largeTitle)
                        .imageScale(.large)
                        .symbolRenderingMode(.hierarchical)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)

                    Text("Good night")
                        .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                    Text("Sleep mode starts in ten minutes.")
                        .font(.callout)
                        .opacity(0.8)
                }
                .foregroundStyle(.white)
                .multilineTextAlignment(.center)
                .padding(36)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                .background(.white.opacity(0.12), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 32))
                .padding(28)
                .transition(.blurFade)
            }
        }
        .task {
            while (try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.3))) != nil {
                withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.6)) { isShown.toggle() }
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    BlurFadeTransitionDemo()
}
```

## Circle Reveal Transition

A custom transition that reveals a view through a circular mask growing from a point.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/CircleRevealTransition/CircleRevealTransition.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A transition that reveals a view through a circle growing from a point.
/// Use it as `.transition(.circleReveal(from: .bottomTrailing))`.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the view fades instead.
struct CircleRevealTransition: Transition {
    var origin: UnitPoint = .center

    func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.modifier(CircleRevealEffect(origin: origin, isIdentity: phase.isIdentity))
    }
}

extension Transition where Self == CircleRevealTransition {
    static func circleReveal(from origin: UnitPoint = .center) -> CircleRevealTransition {
        CircleRevealTransition(origin: origin)
    }
}

enum CircleRevealTransitionGeometry {
    /// The radius of the smallest circle centered on `origin` that covers the whole of `size`.
    static func coverRadius(from origin: UnitPoint, in size: CGSize) -> CGFloat {
        let horizontal = max(origin.x, 1 - origin.x) * size.width
        let vertical = max(origin.y, 1 - origin.y) * size.height
        return hypot(horizontal, vertical)
    }
}

private struct CircleRevealEffect: ViewModifier {
    let origin: UnitPoint
    let isIdentity: Bool

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .clipShape(CircleRevealShape(origin: origin, progress: isIdentity || reduceMotion ? 1 : 0))
            .opacity(reduceMotion && !isIdentity ? 0 : 1)
    }
}

private struct CircleRevealShape: Shape {
    let origin: UnitPoint
    var progress: CGFloat

    var animatableData: CGFloat {
        get { progress }
        set { progress = newValue }
    }

    func path(in rect: CGRect) -> Path {
        let radius = CircleRevealTransitionGeometry.coverRadius(from: origin, in: rect.size) * progress
        let center = CGPoint(x: rect.minX + rect.width * origin.x, y: rect.minY + rect.height * origin.y)
        return Path(ellipseIn: CGRect(x: center.x - radius, y: center.y - radius, width: radius * 2, height: radius * 2))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct CircleRevealTransitionDemo: View {
    @State private var isDark = false

    private let origin = UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0.78)

    var body: some View {
        GeometryReader { proxy in
            ZStack {
                scene(colors: [.cyan, .blue], systemImage: "sun.max.fill", title: "Day")
                    .accessibilityHidden(isDark)

                if isDark {
                    scene(colors: [.indigo, .black], systemImage: "moon.stars.fill", title: "Night")
                        .transition(.circleReveal(from: origin))
                }

                Button(isDark ? "Sunrise" : "Sunset") {
                    withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.8)) { isDark.toggle() }
                }
                .font(.headline)
                .buttonStyle(.bordered)
                .controlSize(.large)
                .tint(.white)
                .position(x: proxy.size.width * origin.x, y: proxy.size.height * origin.y)
            }
        }
        .ignoresSafeArea()
    }

    private func scene(colors: [Color], systemImage: String, title: String) -> some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)

            VStack(spacing: 14) {
                Image(systemName: systemImage)
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, weight: .semibold))
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text(title)
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    CircleRevealTransitionDemo()
}
```

## Content Swap Transition

A showcase of text value changes using numericText, interpolate and opacity content transitions.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/ContentSwapTransition/ContentSwapTransition.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

enum ContentSwapTransitionStyle {
    case numeric(Double)
    case interpolate
    case opacity
}

/// Text that swaps its value with a content transition: rolling digits, a morph or a fade.
/// Change the text inside an animation.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, numbers fade instead of rolling.
struct ContentSwapTransition: View {
    let text: String
    var style: ContentSwapTransitionStyle = .opacity

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var transition: ContentTransition {
        switch style {
        case .numeric(let value): reduceMotion ? .opacity : .numericText(value: value)
        case .interpolate: .interpolate
        case .opacity: .opacity
        }
    }

    var body: some View {
        Text(text)
            .contentTransition(transition)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct ContentSwapTransitionDemo: View {
    @State private var step = 0

    private let amounts: [Double] = [1284, 1317, 2096, 1905]
    private let greetings = ["Hello", "Hola", "Bonjour", "Ciao"]

    private var amount: Double { amounts[step % amounts.count] }
    private var isHeavy: Bool { step.isMultiple(of: 2) }

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 16) {
            card("numericText", systemImage: "number", tint: .blue) {
                ContentSwapTransition(text: amount.formatted(.currency(code: "EUR")), style: .numeric(amount))
            }

            card("interpolate", systemImage: "textformat", tint: .pink) {
                ContentSwapTransition(text: "Weight", style: .interpolate)
                    .fontWeight(isHeavy ? .black : .ultraLight)
                    .foregroundStyle(isHeavy ? .pink : .orange)
            }

            card("opacity", systemImage: "circle.lefthalf.filled", tint: .teal) {
                ContentSwapTransition(text: greetings[step % greetings.count], style: .opacity)
            }
        }
        .padding(20)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground).ignoresSafeArea())
        .task {
            while (try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.2))) != nil {
                withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.6)) { step += 1 }
            }
        }
    }

    private func card(
        _ title: String,
        systemImage: String,
        tint: Color,
        @ViewBuilder content: () -> some View
    ) -> some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 12) {
            Label(title, systemImage: systemImage)
                .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
                .foregroundStyle(tint)

            content()
                .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
                .monospacedDigit()
                .lineLimit(1)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
        }
        .padding(24)
        .background(Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))
    }
}

#Preview {
    ContentSwapTransitionDemo()
}
```

## Cross Fade Navigation

A sheet that fades in over the content with the iOS 27 cross-fade navigation transition.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 27.0. Path: Components/Transitions/CrossFadeNavigation/CrossFadeNavigation.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// Presents a sheet that fades in over the content with the iOS 27 `.crossFade` transition,
/// instead of moving up from the bottom.
///
/// Apple documents `.crossFade` for sheets. Keep `navigationTransition` on the root of the
/// sheet's content, outside any container such as `VStack`. A cross-fade has no movement,
/// so Reduce Motion needs nothing different.
@available(iOS 27, *)
struct CrossFadeNavigation<SheetContent: View>: ViewModifier {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    @ViewBuilder var sheetContent: () -> SheetContent

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content.sheet(isPresented: $isPresented) {
            sheetContent()
                .navigationTransition(.crossFade)
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 27, *)
extension View {
    func crossFadeSheet<SheetContent: View>(
        isPresented: Binding<Bool>,
        @ViewBuilder content: @escaping () -> SheetContent
    ) -> some View {
        modifier(CrossFadeNavigation(isPresented: isPresented, sheetContent: content))
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

@available(iOS 27, *)
struct CrossFadeNavigationDemo: View {
    @State private var showsSheet = false

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.orange, .pink], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 24) {
                Image(systemName: "sunrise.fill")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, weight: .semibold))
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text("Morning")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                Button("Open") { showsSheet = true }
                    .font(.headline)
                    .buttonStyle(.bordered)
                    .controlSize(.large)
                    .tint(.white)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
        .crossFadeSheet(isPresented: $showsSheet) {
            CrossFadeNavigationDemoSheet()
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 27, *)
private struct CrossFadeNavigationDemoSheet: View {
    @Environment(\.dismiss) private var dismiss

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: [.indigo, .black], startPoint: .top, endPoint: .bottom)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 24) {
                Image(systemName: "moon.stars.fill")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, weight: .semibold))
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text("Evening")
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                Button("Close") { dismiss() }
                    .font(.headline)
                    .buttonStyle(.bordered)
                    .controlSize(.large)
                    .tint(.white)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
        }
    }
}

@available(iOS 27, *)
#Preview {
    CrossFadeNavigationDemo()
}
```

## Flip Card Transition

A two-sided card that flips in 3D without ever showing mirrored content.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/FlipCardTransition/FlipCardTransition.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A two-sided card that flips with a 3D rotation when `isFlipped` changes.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the faces swap without rotating.
struct FlipCardTransition<Front: View, Back: View>: View {
    let isFlipped: Bool
    @ViewBuilder var front: () -> Front
    @ViewBuilder var back: () -> Back

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        FlipCardFaces(degrees: isFlipped ? 180 : 0, front: front(), back: back())
            .animation(reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.7), value: isFlipped)
    }
}

// Animatable so the visible face is chosen from the angle on every frame, at the exact
// moment the card is edge-on. A Bool would show a mirrored face for half of the flip.
private struct FlipCardFaces<Front: View, Back: View>: View, Animatable {
    nonisolated var degrees: Double
    let front: Front
    let back: Back

    nonisolated var animatableData: Double {
        get { degrees }
        set { degrees = newValue }
    }

    private var showsFront: Bool { degrees < 90 }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            front
                .opacity(showsFront ? 1 : 0)
                .accessibilityHidden(!showsFront)

            // Turned half way so it reads correctly once the card has turned the other half.
            back
                .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(180), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0))
                .opacity(showsFront ? 0 : 1)
                .accessibilityHidden(showsFront)
        }
        .rotation3DEffect(.degrees(degrees), axis: (x: 0, y: 1, z: 0), perspective: 0.5)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct FlipCardTransitionDemo: View {
    @State private var isFlipped = false
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .title) private var cardHeight = 240.0

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 40) {
            FlipCardTransition(isFlipped: isFlipped) {
                face(colors: [.indigo, .purple]) {
                    Image(systemName: "creditcard.fill")
                        .font(.largeTitle)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                    Text("Membership")
                        .font(.title.bold())
                    Text("Tap Flip to see the back")
                        .font(.subheadline)
                }
            } back: {
                face(colors: [.teal, .mint]) {
                    Image(systemName: "qrcode")
                        .font(.largeTitle)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)
                    Text("No. 2026 0042")
                        .font(.title.monospacedDigit().bold())
                    Text("Valid until December")
                        .font(.subheadline)
                }
            }
            .frame(height: cardHeight)
            .padding(.horizontal, 28)

            Button("Flip", systemImage: "arrow.left.arrow.right") {
                isFlipped.toggle()
            }
            .font(.headline)
            .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
            .controlSize(.large)
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground).ignoresSafeArea())
    }

    private func face(colors: [Color], @ViewBuilder content: () -> some View) -> some View {
        VStack(spacing: 10) {
            content()
        }
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(
            LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing),
            in: .rect(cornerRadius: 28)
        )
    }
}

#Preview {
    FlipCardTransitionDemo()
}
```

## Matched Hero Card

A card that expands in place into a full detail view using matched geometry.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/MatchedHeroCard/MatchedHeroCard.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A card that grows in place to fill its parent, using `matchedGeometryEffect`.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the card changes state without animating.
struct MatchedHeroCard<Detail: View>: View {
    let title: String
    let subtitle: String
    let systemImage: String
    var colors: [Color] = [.indigo, .purple]
    @ViewBuilder var detail: () -> Detail

    @State private var isExpanded = false
    @Namespace private var namespace
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var collapsedHeight = 220.0
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var iconSize = 52.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var animation: Animation? {
        reduceMotion ? nil : .smooth(duration: 0.5, extraBounce: 0.08)
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack(alignment: .top) {
            if isExpanded {
                expandedCard
            } else {
                collapsedCard
            }
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .top)
        .foregroundStyle(.white)
    }

    private var collapsedCard: some View {
        Button {
            withAnimation(animation) { isExpanded = true }
        } label: {
            header
                .padding(24)
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, minHeight: collapsedHeight, alignment: .bottomLeading)
                .background { background }
                .contentShape(.rect)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(title)
        .accessibilityHint("Expands the card")
    }

    private var expandedCard: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 24) {
            header

            detail()
                .transition(.opacity)

            Spacer(minLength: 0)
        }
        .padding(24)
        .padding(.top, 32)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading)
        .background { background }
        .overlay(alignment: .topTrailing) {
            Button {
                withAnimation(animation) { isExpanded = false }
            } label: {
                Image(systemName: "xmark")
                    .font(.headline)
                    .padding(12)
                    .background(.white.opacity(0.2), in: .circle)
            }
            .buttonStyle(.plain)
            .accessibilityLabel("Close")
            .padding(16)
            .transition(.opacity)
        }
    }

    private var header: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
            Image(systemName: systemImage)
                .font(.system(size: iconSize, weight: .semibold))
                .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "icon", in: namespace)
                .accessibilityHidden(true)

            Text(title)
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())
                .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "title", in: namespace)

            Text(subtitle)
                .font(.subheadline)
                .opacity(0.85)
                .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "subtitle", in: namespace)
        }
    }

    private var background: some View {
        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 28, style: .continuous)
            .fill(LinearGradient(colors: colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing))
            .matchedGeometryEffect(id: "background", in: namespace)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct MatchedHeroCardDemo: View {
    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var rowsOffset = 240.0

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 16) {
            Text("Today")
                .font(.largeTitle.bold())

            ZStack(alignment: .top) {
                VStack(spacing: 12) {
                    row("Harbor walk", systemImage: "sailboat.fill")
                    row("Lunch at the market", systemImage: "fork.knife")
                    row("Sunset viewpoint", systemImage: "sun.horizon.fill")
                }
                .padding(.top, rowsOffset)

                MatchedHeroCard(
                    title: "Lisbon",
                    subtitle: "Three days by the river",
                    systemImage: "tram.fill",
                    colors: [.orange, .pink, .purple]
                ) {
                    Text("Tiled streets, yellow trams and the best custard tarts you will ever taste. The card grew from where it was and goes back there when you close it.")
                        .font(.body)
                }
            }
        }
        .padding(20)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity, alignment: .topLeading)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground).ignoresSafeArea())
    }

    private func row(_ title: String, systemImage: String) -> some View {
        Label(title, systemImage: systemImage)
            .font(.headline)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            .padding(18)
            .background(Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 18))
    }
}

#Preview {
    MatchedHeroCardDemo()
}
```

## Slide Scale Transition

A custom transition that combines an offset with a scale, available as .slideScale.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/SlideScaleTransition/SlideScaleTransition.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A transition that slides and scales a view: it enters from one side and leaves by the other.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the view only fades.
struct SlideScaleTransition: Transition {
    var axis: Axis = .horizontal
    var distance: CGFloat = 220
    var scale: CGFloat = 0.8

    func body(content: Content, phase: TransitionPhase) -> some View {
        content.modifier(SlideScaleEffect(axis: axis, distance: distance, scale: scale, phase: phase))
    }
}

extension Transition where Self == SlideScaleTransition {
    static var slideScale: SlideScaleTransition { SlideScaleTransition() }

    static func slideScale(axis: Axis, distance: CGFloat = 220, scale: CGFloat = 0.8) -> SlideScaleTransition {
        SlideScaleTransition(axis: axis, distance: distance, scale: scale)
    }
}

// The effect lives in a view modifier so it can read the environment.
private struct SlideScaleEffect: ViewModifier {
    let axis: Axis
    let distance: CGFloat
    let scale: CGFloat
    let phase: TransitionPhase

    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    // `phase.value` is -1 before appearing, 0 at rest and 1 after disappearing.
    private var offset: CGFloat {
        reduceMotion ? 0 : -phase.value * distance
    }

    func body(content: Content) -> some View {
        content
            .scaleEffect(phase.isIdentity || reduceMotion ? 1 : scale)
            .offset(x: axis == .horizontal ? offset : 0, y: axis == .vertical ? offset : 0)
            .opacity(phase.isIdentity ? 1 : 0)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SlideScaleTransitionDemo: View {
    @State private var index = 0

    private let cards: [(title: String, systemImage: String, colors: [Color])] = [
        ("Run", "figure.run", [.orange, .red]),
        ("Swim", "figure.pool.swim", [.cyan, .blue]),
        ("Climb", "figure.climbing", [.mint, .green]),
    ]

    private var card: (title: String, systemImage: String, colors: [Color]) {
        cards[index % cards.count]
    }

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            Color(.systemGroupedBackground)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 20) {
                Image(systemName: card.systemImage)
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, weight: .semibold))
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text(card.title)
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .frame(height: 340)
            .background(
                LinearGradient(colors: card.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing),
                in: .rect(cornerRadius: 36)
            )
            .padding(32)
            .id(index)
            .transition(.slideScale)
        }
        .task {
            while (try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1.3))) != nil {
                withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.55)) { index += 1 }
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    SlideScaleTransitionDemo()
}
```

## Staggered Appear List

A list whose rows enter one after another with a capped, testable delay.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/StaggeredAppearList/StaggeredAppearList.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

enum StaggeredAppearListTiming {
    /// How long a row waits before it enters. The cap keeps long lists from stalling.
    static func delay(
        forIndex index: Int,
        step: Double = 0.07,
        maximum: Double = 0.6,
        reduceMotion: Bool = false
    ) -> Double {
        guard !reduceMotion else { return 0 }
        return min(max(Double(index), 0) * step, maximum)
    }
}

/// Rows that enter one after another when the list appears.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, every row fades in at once without moving.
struct StaggeredAppearList<Item: Identifiable, Row: View>: View {
    let items: [Item]
    var spacing: CGFloat = 12
    var travel: CGFloat = 28
    @ViewBuilder var row: (Item) -> Row

    @State private var isVisible = false
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: spacing) {
            ForEach(Array(items.enumerated()), id: \.element.id) { index, item in
                row(item)
                    .opacity(isVisible ? 1 : 0)
                    .offset(y: isVisible || reduceMotion ? 0 : travel)
                    .animation(
                        .smooth(duration: 0.45)
                            .delay(StaggeredAppearListTiming.delay(forIndex: index, reduceMotion: reduceMotion)),
                        value: isVisible
                    )
            }
        }
        .onAppear { isVisible = true }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct StaggeredAppearDemoRow: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let detail: String
    let systemImage: String
    let tint: Color
}

struct StaggeredAppearListDemo: View {
    @State private var replay = 0

    private let rows = [
        StaggeredAppearDemoRow(id: "Inbox", detail: "12 new messages", systemImage: "tray.fill", tint: .blue),
        StaggeredAppearDemoRow(id: "Calendar", detail: "Standup at 9:30", systemImage: "calendar", tint: .red),
        StaggeredAppearDemoRow(id: "Music", detail: "Your weekly mix", systemImage: "music.note", tint: .pink),
        StaggeredAppearDemoRow(id: "Photos", detail: "48 added today", systemImage: "photo.fill", tint: .orange),
        StaggeredAppearDemoRow(id: "Health", detail: "6,204 steps", systemImage: "heart.fill", tint: .green),
        StaggeredAppearDemoRow(id: "Files", detail: "2 shared with you", systemImage: "folder.fill", tint: .teal),
        StaggeredAppearDemoRow(id: "Notes", detail: "Groceries, ideas", systemImage: "note.text", tint: .yellow),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            StaggeredAppearList(items: rows) { row in
                HStack(spacing: 14) {
                    Image(systemName: row.systemImage)
                        .font(.title3)
                        .foregroundStyle(row.tint)
                        .frame(width: 36)
                        .accessibilityHidden(true)

                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
                        Text(row.id)
                            .font(.headline)
                        Text(row.detail)
                            .font(.subheadline)
                            .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
                    }

                    Spacer(minLength: 0)
                }
                .padding(16)
                .background(Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 18))
            }
            .id(replay)
            .padding(20)
        }
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground).ignoresSafeArea())
        .task {
            while (try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(2.4))) != nil {
                replay += 1
            }
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    StaggeredAppearListDemo()
}
```

## Symbol Morph Toggle

A toggle whose SF Symbol morphs between states with the iOS 18 magic replace effect.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/SymbolMorphToggle/SymbolMorphToggle.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A toggle whose SF Symbol morphs between two states with the magic replace effect.
/// The magic effect shows between related symbols, such as `bell.fill` and `bell.slash.fill`.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the symbols fade.
struct SymbolMorphToggle: View {
    let title: String
    let onSymbol: String
    let offSymbol: String
    @Binding var isOn: Bool
    var tint: Color = .blue

    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle) private var symbolSize = 44.0
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    private var transition: ContentTransition {
        reduceMotion ? .opacity : .symbolEffect(.replace.magic(fallback: .downUp.byLayer))
    }

    var body: some View {
        Button {
            withAnimation(.smooth(duration: 0.4)) { isOn.toggle() }
        } label: {
            VStack(spacing: 12) {
                Image(systemName: isOn ? onSymbol : offSymbol)
                    .font(.system(size: symbolSize, weight: .medium))
                    .symbolRenderingMode(.hierarchical)
                    .contentTransition(transition)
                    .frame(height: symbolSize * 1.3)
                    .foregroundStyle(isOn ? tint : .secondary)

                Text(title)
                    .font(.headline)
            }
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
            .padding(.vertical, 28)
            .background(Color(.secondarySystemGroupedBackground), in: .rect(cornerRadius: 24))
            .contentShape(.rect)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(title)
        .accessibilityValue(isOn ? "On" : "Off")
        .accessibilityAddTraits(.isToggle)
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

struct SymbolMorphToggleDemo: View {
    @State private var alerts = true
    @State private var microphone = true
    @State private var camera = true
    @State private var network = true

    var body: some View {
        Grid(horizontalSpacing: 14, verticalSpacing: 14) {
            GridRow {
                SymbolMorphToggle(title: "Alerts", onSymbol: "bell.fill", offSymbol: "bell.slash.fill", isOn: $alerts, tint: .orange)
                SymbolMorphToggle(title: "Microphone", onSymbol: "mic.fill", offSymbol: "mic.slash.fill", isOn: $microphone, tint: .pink)
            }

            GridRow {
                SymbolMorphToggle(title: "Camera", onSymbol: "video.fill", offSymbol: "video.slash.fill", isOn: $camera, tint: .green)
                SymbolMorphToggle(title: "Network", onSymbol: "wifi", offSymbol: "wifi.slash", isOn: $network, tint: .blue)
            }
        }
        .padding(20)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .background(Color(.systemGroupedBackground).ignoresSafeArea())
    }
}

#Preview {
    SymbolMorphToggleDemo()
}
```

## Zoom Hero Transition

A grid of cards that zoom into their detail screen with the native navigation zoom transition.

Category: Transitions. Minimum: iOS 18.0. Path: Components/Transitions/ZoomHeroTransition/ZoomHeroTransition.swift

```swift
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Copyright (c) 2026 Oscar Canton and AwesomeSwiftUI contributors

import SwiftUI

/// A grid of cards that zoom into their detail screen. Place it inside a `NavigationStack`.
///
/// With Reduce Motion on, the detail opens with the standard navigation transition.
struct ZoomHeroTransition<Item: Identifiable & Hashable, Card: View, Detail: View>: View {
    let items: [Item]
    var columns: Int = 2
    var cornerRadius: CGFloat = 24
    @ViewBuilder var card: (Item) -> Card
    @ViewBuilder var detail: (Item) -> Detail

    @Namespace private var namespace
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion

    var body: some View {
        ScrollView {
            LazyVGrid(columns: Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: 14), count: columns), spacing: 14) {
                ForEach(items) { item in
                    NavigationLink(value: item) {
                        card(item)
                            .clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
                            .matchedTransitionSource(id: item.id, in: namespace) { source in
                                source.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: cornerRadius))
                            }
                    }
                    .buttonStyle(.plain)
                }
            }
            .padding(16)
        }
        .navigationDestination(for: Item.self) { item in
            destination(for: item)
        }
    }

    // `.zoom` and `.automatic` are different types, so a ternary cannot choose between them on iOS 18.
    @ViewBuilder
    private func destination(for item: Item) -> some View {
        if reduceMotion {
            detail(item)
        } else {
            detail(item).navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID: item.id, in: namespace))
        }
    }
}

// MARK: - Demo

private struct ZoomHeroDemoPlace: Identifiable, Hashable {
    let id: String
    let systemImage: String
    let colors: [Color]
}

struct ZoomHeroTransitionDemo: View {
    private let places = [
        ZoomHeroDemoPlace(id: "Aurora", systemImage: "sparkles", colors: [.indigo, .teal]),
        ZoomHeroDemoPlace(id: "Dunes", systemImage: "sun.max.fill", colors: [.orange, .pink]),
        ZoomHeroDemoPlace(id: "Forest", systemImage: "leaf.fill", colors: [.green, .mint]),
        ZoomHeroDemoPlace(id: "Glacier", systemImage: "snowflake", colors: [.cyan, .blue]),
        ZoomHeroDemoPlace(id: "Volcano", systemImage: "flame.fill", colors: [.red, .orange]),
        ZoomHeroDemoPlace(id: "Night", systemImage: "moon.stars.fill", colors: [.purple, .indigo]),
    ]

    var body: some View {
        NavigationStack {
            ZoomHeroTransition(items: places) { place in
                LinearGradient(colors: place.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                    .aspectRatio(0.78, contentMode: .fit)
                    .overlay {
                        Image(systemName: place.systemImage)
                            .font(.largeTitle)
                            .imageScale(.large)
                            .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.9))
                            .accessibilityHidden(true)
                    }
                    .overlay(alignment: .bottomLeading) {
                        Text(place.id)
                            .font(.headline)
                            .foregroundStyle(.white)
                            .padding(14)
                    }
            } detail: { place in
                ZoomHeroDemoDetail(place: place)
            }
            .navigationTitle("Places")
        }
    }
}

private struct ZoomHeroDemoDetail: View {
    let place: ZoomHeroDemoPlace

    @Environment(\.dismiss) private var dismiss

    var body: some View {
        ZStack {
            LinearGradient(colors: place.colors, startPoint: .topLeading, endPoint: .bottomTrailing)
                .ignoresSafeArea()

            VStack(spacing: 18) {
                Image(systemName: place.systemImage)
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, weight: .semibold))
                    .imageScale(.large)
                    .accessibilityHidden(true)

                Text(place.id)
                    .font(.system(.largeTitle, design: .rounded, weight: .bold))

                Text("The card grew into this screen. Swipe down or tap Close to send it back.")
                    .font(.body)
                    .multilineTextAlignment(.center)

                Button("Close") { dismiss() }
                    .buttonStyle(.bordered)
                    .tint(.white)
            }
            .foregroundStyle(.white)
            .padding(32)
        }
    }
}

#Preview {
    ZoomHeroTransitionDemo()
}
```
